P11.evidence: A close was attempted — both tiers were priced and the rep asked 'Which one are you leaning towards?' — but no agreement to pay was obtained, so payment collection, the Trevor onboarding booking, the agreement signature and the welcome-email walkthrough were all unreachable on this call. Scored N/A rather than miss so the phase does not double-count the unresolved money objection.

objection_plays.detail: Trigger explicit: 'I just need to check with my girlfriend.' The rep opened correctly with the money-aside isolation — 'money aside, like, do you personally feel that this can get you [there]?' — and it produced the strongest value statement of the call: '100% have someone to coach me... It would be huge, because then I have guidance.' He then made a good unscripted move, asking her to join live: 'Can you get her on a call right now? We can talk right now.' That is the right instinct and it deserves credit. Everything after that stopped. Not run: 'when you talk to her, what obstacles might come up' (which would have surfaced the unknown chemo costs before they became the reason), 'is there any reason she would NOT want you stronger and less in pain', and the deposit-plus-full-refund fallback, which is precisely the structure this situation called for. Note one scripted move that should NOT have been run and correctly was not: 'is this genuinely needing her input, or asking permission to bet on yourself' would have been wrong here, because she demonstrably controls the accounts — 'she's the one that takes care of the bills' — and she is the one who sought Primal out in the first place. She is a decision-maker, not a permission gate, and the play does not distinguish the two.

Two moves run well, then the play collapsed. The should-versus-how reframe was executed almost to the letter: 'So we're talking purely logistics, not like, should I do it, but actually how to do it in terms of finances?' The payment-plan door was opened: 'there are ways that we can move around with finances. If the payment in one installment is difficult, we can work around and maybe split it.' Then the rep inverted the play — 'But I would need to know from you what level of investments you can commit to at the beginning' — which asks the prospect to price himself instead of the rep discovering the picture. The financial picture was never taken: one abandoned question ('do you want to check, like, your checking account? Like, how much do you have?') and then nothing. Not asked: what is left over each month after bills, how many credit cards, available credit per card, used versus available, crypto/stocks/investments. Worst of all, when the prospect asked directly for something concrete — 'if you can send me maybe a few options of how can we pay it or if there is payment plan' — the answer was 'we don't have, like, a set payment plans.' The one artifact that could have moved this deal was requested and refused.

Soft trigger, and worth recording as soft: 'we are really keen. We just cannot give you an answer right now because we need to check the finances... So we're going to think.' No moves ran. In fairness this is closer to a genuine information-gathering delay than a stall — he needs actual balances from the person who holds them — so the full Objection A treatment would have been misapplied. But the two openers still had a place and were not used: 'do you feel what we've gone through CAN get you to [goal]?' had already been answered yes, and 'so what's actually coming up that's preventing you from getting started?' would have cost nothing.

SCRIPT GAP — clinical fit, in the most serious form the corpus has produced. The prospect is eight weeks post-craniotomy, at session 18 of 33 radiotherapy sessions, and beginning twelve months of chemotherapy in seven weeks. He is being sold six to twelve months of loaded ballistic kettlebell training. Nobody on either side of the call asked whether his oncologist, surgeon or physio has cleared him for it; the rep did not raise it and the playbook does not require it. This is the same gap already logged from the Tyron G. call, but there the clinician had at least been consulted. Here the question was never asked at all. Compounding it: the prospect disclosed active distrust of his medical team — 'those doctors, when are you dead? So you've got to do a bit by yourself... They don't let me take anything' — and the rep affirmed the frame rather than treating it as a flag. A mandatory clearance question belongs in Phase 2 and does not currently exist.

SCRIPT GAP — an unbounded and unknowable competing financial obligation. Bruno's objection was not that he lacks money, it was that he cannot size the decision: 'the amount of money that we're going to have to pay for the chemo, we are not really sure yet of the exams, how often we're going to have to do blood tests. So it's hard to commit for, like, big investments when you have something like I do.' Objection C is built for a prospect whose finances are knowable and merely inconvenient; every one of its financial-picture questions assumes a fixed denominator. There is no move for a prospect facing a real, dated, open-ended liability. The obvious answers — a smaller first instalment, a start date deferred into the four-week gap before chemo, a refundable deposit to hold the price — are all available in principle and none is in the script. Worth building; this shape will recur with any prospect in active medical treatment.

SCRIPT GAP — the nutrition pillar has no handling for a therapeutic diet. Bruno is eight weeks into strict keto as part of his cancer strategy. The rep delivered the standard pillar including the weekly balance day: 'once a week, you're going to have like a, quote unquote, like a day off. It's not a cheat meal... But you can have a pizza or something like that, just for mind's sound.' That breaks ketosis, and it was offered to a man whose diet is a deliberate part of an oncology protocol. He accepted it without objection, which means nothing corrected it. The pillar script needs a branch that recognises a medically motivated diet and holds it fixed rather than layering the standard structure over it.

adherence.notes: Two genuinely strong phases — the baseline questioning (P2) and, unusually for this batch, a properly sequenced commitment check (P6) taken before any price was named — sitting either side of a root-cause phase that was not run at all. The commercial failure is narrow and fixable: the money objection was isolated correctly and then abandoned at the exact point the play gets useful, and the prospect's direct request for written payment options was declined, so the person who actually controls the money received nothing to look at. For the follow-up: bring a costed instalment structure, propose a start date in the four-week window between radiotherapy and chemo, and get the girlfriend on the call, since she initiated the enquiry and holds the accounts. Separately, and above the sales coaching: this call needs a policy decision, not a coaching note. There is no clinical clearance step anywhere in the process, and the rep sold six to twelve months of loaded kettlebell work to a man mid-radiotherapy for aggressive brain cancer without anyone asking a doctor. The playbook also has no answer for what the consequence frame becomes when the consequence is a terminal prognosis, and the rep was left to improvise 'version 2.0 of Bruno that kicks the [expletive] of the cancer' on his own.

source.display_title: 05/26/2026 - Jorge Fernández  x Andrew Musial  — Lost

setter.evidence: No KFS/KL/DH suffix in the title and no setter named. The lead came from an Instagram ad that the prospect did not seek out — 'Instagram, I don't remember the name of the guy. Trevor. Maybe, I don't know... it popped up' — and he was not a follower. Whoever booked it set no expectation whatsoever: he opened the call with 'I don't know what I'm doing here. I don't know what this is, actually.'

prospect.name: Jorge Fernández
prospect.location: in Italy at the time of the call, staying rent-free in his wife's aunt's house; returning to Mexico in two months
prospect.occupation: Not established. He self-identifies as a business owner or operator — 'I understand the way this works, I do this for a living as well' and 'you're a businessman, I'm a business guy too' — and says 'I work a lot', but the rep never asked what he actually does. The 'Tualo' suffix on his Zoom label suggests a company affiliation, unverified on the call.
prospect.family_status: Married, travelling with his wife and two daughters aged three and one. His father is 75 and, in his words, 'looks 95' and is 'a crippled old guy' who never exercised. His father-in-law is the same age, exercises a lot, and is 'amazing'. The contrast is his stated motivator.
prospect.training_background: Effectively none. 'I've never been in a good shape, ever' and 'I've never, ever done any exercise', no sport ever played. Three prior attempts, each abandoned at roughly two weeks: a high-school programme with a friend, a gym routine plus a nutritionist, and a Better Me app subscription restarted when his first child was born. Currently three weeks into self-directed YouTube calisthenics at home, around 30 minutes a session — the longest streak of his life.

signals: Anchored to a cheaper alternative that is genuinely working: three weeks of free YouTube calisthenics, the longest he has ever sustained anything, and he said so as an explicit head-to-head — 'if we compare them, they're both at home. Amazing. They're both easy and quick. Amazing... But one of them is free. That's, I think, more amazing than the rest.'

Self-directed by choice and by constraint: 'The reason why I've been training the last three weeks and I'm planning to do it by myself is because I don't have the budget to pay somebody to follow me.'

Explicitly conceded the value and still refused the price, which is the signature of this avatar rather than a value objection — he agreed the coaching layer works ('Definitely. I definitely agree') and bought none of it.

Wants a cheap way to test commitment before committing capital, stated as a fully worked analogy: 'I would first go and buy a small, used bicycle... and then ride it a bit, and then see if I really like it, and then see if that's really a priority... and after a year, then I'll see if I'm prepared to spend 6k, but not now.'

COUNTER-SIGNAL: he is not price-shopping a market — he had no competing quote and no idea of the price band ('Sounds expensive. That's what I'm waiting to hear'). His reference point for a fitness purchase is a $25 tub of protein powder. He is closer to a non-buyer than a bargain hunter, and 'other / never_bought_fitness' was considered; skeptical_bargain_hunter was kept because the free-alternative comparison drove the whole decision.

goals.text: Build muscle and see a visible physical change within the three-month travel window — 'I decided that I wanted to use this three-month travel to build muscle and exercise'
Prove to himself he can look good — 'One is to prove myself that I can look better and be better. Look at myself in the mirror and say, hey, I can do this'
Make a better impression physically — 'whenever somebody looks at me, I'll make a better impression regarding my physique'

Be healthier and push back the onset of age-related decline — 'increasing the chances that health issues don't arise as soon, and that my crippling regarding old age down the road extends as much as possible'
Not end up like his father, who is 75, 'looks 95' and never exercised — and to end up like his father-in-law, the same age and 'amazing', who does
Be able to keep up with two daughters aged three and one — 'They make me exercise even if I don't want to'
Get the best shape of his life now, before it gets harder — 'if I don't do it today, then tomorrow will be harder than yesterday... I'll die never having seen what that could have been like'
Train mobility and movement, not just muscle — the specific thing that made him take the call

pains.text: Three prior attempts, all abandoned at about two weeks — high school programme, gym plus nutritionist, and the Better Me app restarted when his first child was born
Does not enjoy training enough to prioritise it — 'It's that I don't like it enough. So not to make it into my schedule, definitely. I'd rather watch a TV series than work out'

No idea whether he is executing movements correctly — 'I do a push-up, and I'm thinking, like, damn, I have no idea if I did this push-up the right way or not... I feel like I'm doing it but I'm not sure'
Nobody correcting or following him up — 'if there was somebody standing right next to me telling me like, hey, no, those legs aren't straight, I'd be correcting them, but I don't have it'
Works a lot and would rather spend spare time with his family than in a gym — 'I've always said that I have no time to exercise, because it's something that takes a lot of time'
Acute awareness that the window is closing at 34 — 'I'm starting in a point of my life where I'm going down, regarding my best physical age'
Very lean ectomorph who has held the same weight since he was 15 and has never been able to build — 'no matter how much I eat, I'll never... I've been having the same weight since I was 15'
Dislikes gyms outright, which rules out the conventional route — 'going to the gym, for me, it's like, it doesn't make sense for me, at least. And I respect it, but I don't like it'
No liquid cash — travelling, credit cards already committed to flights, no budget for coaching of any kind

objections.raw_quote: Sounds expensive. That's what I'm waiting to hear.
objections.rep_response: Did not address the price signal at all. He ran the pre-close belief question instead ('If you had the right training, a simple nutrition, and someone like Trevor in your corner... would you agree that you would get to your goal?'), got a yes, and moved to explaining delivery. The prospect had to interrupt the onboarding logistics to force the number out: 'Before that, I'd like to understand the full picture. It sounds expensive.'

objections.raw_quote: I don't think it's something I can afford. But I don't know what would be the next step. Like, for me to think about it and give you an answer? Or how does it go?
objections.rep_response: Refused the drift to a think-about-it and isolated immediately — 'finances aside, are you 100% sure that you can actually achieve your goals with Trevor?' then 'Is there anything else holding you back?' He then pushed on what 'no money' actually meant ('you're a businessman, I'm a business guy too... you don't have the full amount?'), got permission for an open financial conversation, and took a partial financial picture: liquid cash (zero), credit card usage, credit score. He offered a financing partner. He did not ask monthly surplus after bills, how many cards, available credit per card, used versus available, or investments — which are the questions that would have determined whether financing was actually viable for someone with zero cash.

objections.raw_quote: if we compare them, they're both at home. Amazing. They're both easy and quick. Amazing. They both give you more strength. Amazing. One of them also gives you the mobility and that sounds super amazing. One of them also has somebody that's following you up and giving you personal assistance and motivation and personalizing the training and the nutrition and whatever. Super amazing. That sounds amazing. But one of them is free. That's, I think, more amazing than the rest. I'm going to be honest.
objections.rep_response: Improvised, and largely conceded the ground. He agreed the content is free — 'Everything, all the knowledge, everything, it's on YouTube. You can look it up' — which handed the prospect his own argument ('Yeah, that's exactly my point'). He then made the only correct move available, differentiating on accountability and programming: 'the difference is in the accountability, especially' and 'if you haven't been like a gym rat or working out for 10 years, setting up a proper plan...'. The prospect fully agreed with the differentiation and still would not pay. There is no scripted play for this objection.

objections.raw_quote: if I was, like, a year into it, and I knew this was something I was really invested in, it's like, I don't know, wanting to starting to learn how to bike, and after two seconds, going and buying a mountain bike that's 6k. I would never do that. I would first go and buy a small, used bicycle... and then after a year, then I'll see if I'm prepared to spend 6k, but not now.
objections.rep_response: Agreed with it and closed the call out: 'Yeah, yeah, makes sense. Look, maybe it's not the time of the, not the right time in your life for these changes.' Objection D was not run in any form. Notably, the prospect had himself argued the exact opposite thirty-five minutes earlier — 'every day that passes from now on, it's harder, not easier... if I don't do it today, then tomorrow will be harder than yesterday' — and the rep did not use it.

objections.raw_quote: As I told you before, I don't know if specifically Trevor, but like you said, if there's...
objections.rep_response: Glossed over it. The rep treated the answer as a yes and moved straight to 'so we're not talking about the money is the only obstacle right now from proceeding.' The prospect had just said he could not distinguish this coach from any competent coach, which is a live differentiation problem and, strictly, means the isolation was never cleanly achieved.

offer.payment_plan_terms: No structured plan. The rep stated 'we don't have anything set in stone, like payment plans, but if there's a will, there's a way' and then offered a third-party financing partner. No amounts, terms or schedule were named, and the prospect declined the concept outright.

evidence: Explicit refusal of the offer and of financing: 'So, for 6k? No. Because it's not something I would ever pay 6k for.'

The rep disqualified rather than discounted, and said so: 'Look, maybe it's not the time of the, not the right time in your life for these changes.' The prospect accepted it — 'Everything sounds amazing, but I knew it was something that was gonna be difficult... I suspected that was the case.'
Parted cleanly with no next step, no follow-up call, and no artifact to send: 'no hard feelings, like I said at the beginning. If it's alignment, it's cool. If not, no worries.'

The prospect had conceded the value entirely before refusing, which makes this a pure affordability and priority loss rather than a value loss: 'That would definitely improve my chances of getting there. As you just said, the equation sounds amazing. But there's a fourth ingredient there. That's the money.'

He also self-disqualified on priority under questioning, which the rep drew out well: 'I pay Netflix, because I love movies. And I pay delicious food... But that's a priority for me. My physique... not that much.'

Counter-evidence worth recording: intent was real and current, not theoretical — three weeks into self-directed training, the longest streak of his life, protein and creatine bought that week, and an articulate motivational stack around his father's decline and two young daughters. This was a genuinely motivated prospect with zero money.
outcome.next_step: None. Call ended as a mutual, amicable disqualification with no follow-up scheduled and nothing sent.

notable.note: The cleanest disqualification in the batch and, on process, one of the better-run calls — but it exposes three things worth escalating. (1) FUNNEL, not rep: the prospect arrived from an Instagram ad he had not sought out, was not a follower of Trevor, and opened with 'I don't know what I'm doing here. I don't know what this is, actually.' Nobody set an expectation of price, format or seriousness before the call. Forty-three minutes of a closer's time went to someone with zero liquid cash whose reference point for a fitness purchase is a $25 tub of protein powder. That is a targeting and qualification problem upstream. (2) The free-alternative objection now has its extreme case on record. The known script gap was written around a $29/month coach; here the competing product costs nothing, is currently working, and the prospect built the comparison himself, feature by feature, conceding every point of superiority and still choosing free. The rep's only counter — accountability and programming — was agreed with and did not move him. (3) The single biggest coaching miss is a gift the rep left on the table: at 00:07:28 Jorge argued the Objection D rebuttal himself, unprompted — 'if I don't do it today, then tomorrow will be harder than yesterday' — and at 00:41:21, when he said 'after a year, then I'll see if I'm prepared to spend 6k, but not now', the rep agreed with him instead of quoting his own words back. Separately: the rep asked for a credit score and accepted 'Amazing. 10.' as an answer, then offered financing on that basis. Pricing was quoted correctly at $6,000 for six months on this call — worth contrasting with the $4,000 three-month tier the same rep quoted the previous day.

quality.notes: Heavy inversion throughout; roles read from content. Clear examples: at 00:04:21 'It's called ectomorph' is attributed to the prospect but is obviously the rep supplying the term, and the height exchange immediately after is inverted so that 'And how tall are you?' sits under the prospect's label; at 00:10:23 'Three and one' (the daughters' ages) sits under the rep's label but is the prospect's answer; the entire block from roughly 00:37:00 to 00:38:00 runs as one undifferentiated paragraph under a single label containing both sides of the exchange; and at 00:41:00-00:41:09 the credit-card and credit-score questions and answers are swapped, so 'what's your credit score?' lands under the prospect and 'Amazing. 10.' lands under him too. There is also a ~2.5 minute gap at the start (00:00:15 to 00:02:39) with connection setup, and a freeze around 00:32:24. Several passages contain untranscribable ASR garbage ('lost lost Spebaum No the And But And', '과どう they with What What What's What'). The rep's display label reads 'Andrew Jin (Primal Instinct)' while the title and folder say Andrew Musial; recorded as Andrew Musial, flagged for confirmation.

P1.evidence: P1a miss, with unusually direct evidence: nothing was read back and the prospect opened with 'I don't know what I'm doing here. I don't know what this is, actually.' The rep recovered well — 'These calls are very simple' — but the check is about making them feel seen from their own application, and there was no application in the room. P1b partial: three of four parts — 'I just want to understand what's going on, what have you tried, and where you're trying to get to in terms of fitness, health.' 'What you need' was not framed. He did add a clean takeaway — 'if there's alignment, we can talk about it, for sure. If not, that's fine, too' — which he then honoured at the end. P1c hit: 'Sounds good?' asked and agreed. P1d hit: 'walk me through, like, what's been going on? Like, what's the main thing you're trying to fix now?', preceded by a good source question, 'How did you actually found out about us?'

P2.evidence: The weakest baseline in the batch. P2a partial — height was asked ('And how tall are you?') and weight was volunteered and echoed; age was volunteered ('I'm 34 now') and never asked. P2b miss, and consequential: the rep never asked what he does for work, yet twice asserted 'you're a businessman, I'm a business guy too' and built the whole money conversation on that assumption. For a prospect who turned out to have zero liquid cash, establishing the actual occupation and income was the one baseline question that would have changed the call. P2c and P2d miss — no health conditions, no injuries, no movement limitations, on a 34-year-old who has never exercised in his life and is about to be sold ballistic loaded training. P2e miss — the current calisthenics routine and its frequency were volunteered ('Calisthenics is also like 30 minute workout and it's in my house'), never asked. P2f miss — three weeks in, and the rep never asked what results he was already getting, which would have been the natural setup for the free-alternative objection that later killed the deal. P2g hit and genuinely good — 'how about nutrition? How do you treat your body?', then 'do you follow any diets?', then careful clarification of the vegetarian boundaries including fish, eggs and dairy. P2h and P2i miss — sleep and energy never raised, though the rep later asserted energy benefits he had no baseline for.

P3.evidence: The strongest questioning in the call, and it still failed at the decisive check. P3a hit — 'what's the main thing you're trying to fix now?' P3b and P3c miss — the mobility/strength/energy menu was never offered and the 'something you want to do but can't' question was never asked. P3d hit, run twice and well: 'Sorry to cut you off, but like, why is that so important to you?' and when the answer was 'I don't know', he held the silence — 'Just think about it for a second. What's the reason that you actually want to get in shape? Why?' That produced the mirror answer and the health answer. P3e hit — 'in three months, or let's say six months down the road, when you actually see the changes in your body... what opens up to you?', and when Jorge said he did not understand the question, the rep rephrased rather than dropping it. P3f partial — the impact on others was asserted rather than asked: 'So you want to show up for them. So every single day when you wake up and you see their faces, you know what's your why behind that.' P3g hit — the rep drove to longevity and legacy properly, using the father contrast and then the sit-to-stand longevity test: 'if you want to be at 75 and be supple... this is a scientific measurement of your longevity.' P3h miss, and this is where the call was actually lost. The reflect-back never happened because the prospect refused to supply a deep why: 'It won't change my life. That's what I mean' and 'No, definitely not.' The rep pushed once — 'Do you really believe that if you change your body, how you feel with your body, how you show up, that won't change your life?' — got 'it's just gonna add something to my personal profile', and then capitulated: 'I like it. That's good enough.' It was not good enough. The prospect had just told him the outcome was worth about as much as learning French or taking up chess, and the rep proceeded to a $6,000 ask on that basis.

P4.evidence: The best-run root-cause phase in the batch by some distance. P4a hit — asked in the frame and pursued with 'Never?', producing a detailed three-attempt history. P4b partial — the outcomes were narrated rather than elicited; the rep never asked 'what happened with that' directly. P4c hit — 'have you thought about deep down what's been behind that, that you didn't enjoy or wanted to actually make that change in the past?' P4d hit, and the best single move on the call: when Jorge gave the standard excuse ('I have no time to exercise'), the rep declined to accept it — 'Well, it depends. We're all busy, yeah?' — and that pressure produced the truth: 'It's that I don't like it enough... I'd rather watch a TV series than work out.' That is the actual obstacle, surfaced properly. P4e partial — having got there, the rep did not let Jorge name the structural gap; he pivoted straight into a kettlebell feature pitch ('So the beauty about kettlebells is you can do it in home...'). The gap he needed named — no accountability, no programming — went unnamed until the prospect raised it himself during the price objection. P4f partial — the line exists in the script almost for this exact prospect, who is currently self-coaching from YouTube, and it was run reactively at 00:36:26 ('the difference is in the accountability, especially') rather than in Phase 4 where it would have built the case before the number.

P5.evidence: The consequence frame was never built, and the material for it was exceptional. The prospect handed over a fully formed two-year picture unprompted — a father who is 75, 'looks 95', never exercised and is now 'a crippled old guy', set against a father-in-law of the same age who trains and is 'amazing' — plus his own line, 'if I don't do it today, then tomorrow will be harder than yesterday.' P5a miss: 'if nothing changes, what does life look like' was never asked, and with that father sitting in the conversation it would have written itself. P5b and P5c miss: no settling question, no 'why not'. P5d partial: the rep used the exact scripted phrase — 'So this is the, like, the moment of drawing the line in the sand. And like, I'm doing something and not just talking about it' — but ran it at 00:38:54, after the price and after the prospect had already said he had no money, where it read as pressure rather than as a decision point. Phase 5 exists to make the price feel small before the price is named; here it arrived after, and did nothing.

P6.evidence: P6a hit and correctly sequenced before the number: 'If you had the right training, a simple nutrition, and someone like Trevor in your corner, all built around your life actually, would you agree that you would get to your goal?' Answer: 'definitely.' P6b partial — the go-all-in question was never asked before presenting; its nearest equivalent, 'Is there anything else holding you back?', ran at 00:34:31, after price, as objection isolation. And the answer it produced was contaminated: seconds earlier Jorge had said 'I don't know if specifically Trevor', which the rep treated as a yes and moved past, so the isolation was never clean. P6c miss, and it is the structural failure of the call. The script says move forward only on a clear yes and return to Phase 5 if hesitation surfaces. Hesitation had surfaced twice and been ignored: the prospect explicitly rejected the deep why ('It won't change my life'), and then flagged the price before it was named ('Sounds expensive. That's what I'm waiting to hear'). The rep proceeded through the delivery walkthrough and into the number both times, and never went back to Phase 5.

P11.evidence: The deal never reached the phase — the prospect refused the offer and the financing outright, so payment, onboarding, agreement and welcome-email steps were all unreachable. Worth recording as a sequencing note rather than a score, though: the rep attempted step 2 before step 1 and before the price existed. At 00:32:35 he said 'next thing is we need to book you with Trevor', and the prospect had to interrupt to stop him — 'Before that, I'd like to understand the full picture. It sounds expensive.' Booking the onboarding call before naming the number, and before any payment, inverts the phase.

objection_plays.detail: The most complete Objection C run in this batch, and still only half the play. Ran correctly: ISOLATE FIRST — 'finances aside, are you 100% sure that you can actually achieve your goals with Trevor?' and 'Is there anything else holding you back?'; the should-versus-how reframe in the rep's own idiom — 'We're business guys, we can work things out, yeah? So we don't have anything set in stone, like payment plans, but if there's a will, there's a way'; permission for the financial conversation, close to verbatim — 'So you're open for an open discussion about finances?'; and then three of the six financial-picture items — liquid cash ('what's your liquid cash right now on your hand?', answer zero), credit card usage, and credit score. He also pushed properly on the vague claim rather than accepting it: 'when you say you don't have money, what do you exactly mean by that? You don't have the full amount?' Not run: what is left over each month after bills, how many credit cards, available credit total per card, and used versus available — which are precisely the questions that determine whether a financing partner can do anything for a man with zero cash. Investments were also never asked. Two flaws beyond omission. First, the isolation was not clean: 'I don't know if specifically Trevor' was treated as a yes. Second, the rep offered financing on the back of a credit-score answer of 'Amazing. 10.', which is not a credit score on any scale and was not clarified.

Trigger present in substance and at length — the mountain-bike analogy is a textbook not-the-right-time: 'I would first go and buy a small, used bicycle... and then after a year, then I'll see if I'm prepared to spend 6k, but not now.' The rep ran the play in reverse. He agreed with it and then volunteered the objection on the prospect's behalf: 'Yeah, yeah, makes sense. Look, maybe it's not the time of the, not the right time in your life for these changes.' None of the six moves ran. The omission that matters most: 'the longer you wait the harder this gets' was the prospect's own thesis, delivered unprompted at 00:07:28 — 'I'm 34. I'm not 24 anymore. And if I don't do it right now, every day that passes from now on, it's harder, not easier, as it was before.' The rep had a written rebuttal in the prospect's own words, thirty-five minutes old, and did not reach for it. In fairness, the disqualification may well have been the correct commercial judgement given zero cash; the play still should have run before conceding.

Soft trigger and a credit to the rep: the prospect reached for the delay himself — 'I don't know what would be the next step. Like, for me to think about it and give you an answer? Or how does it go?' — and the rep refused to grant it, going straight to the isolation question instead. That is the right instinct and the right sequence. It scores partial rather than hit because none of the Objection A follow-through ran once the isolation was answered: no 'what makes you feel it can', no 'thinking isn't the problem, deciding is', no 'the way you've been approaching this brought you here — when do you make a different decision', which had obvious purchase on a man with three abandoned attempts behind him.

SCRIPT GAP, and the extreme case of the one already logged. The known gap covers 'a cheaper alternative already worked for me' as seen with a $29/month coach. Here the alternative is free YouTube calisthenics, it is currently working — three weeks, the longest streak of the prospect's life — and he constructed the comparison himself, feature by feature, conceding every point of Primal's superiority before choosing free anyway: 'One of them also has somebody that's following you up... Super amazing. That sounds amazing. But one of them is free. That's, I think, more amazing than the rest.' The rep improvised the only sensible line, differentiating on accountability and programming rather than content, and it earns the partial. But he opened by conceding the content is free ('Everything, all the knowledge, everything, it's on YouTube. You can look it up'), which handed the prospect his own case — 'Yeah, that's exactly my point.' Objection C cannot touch this, because the blocker is not capacity to pay; it is a functioning zero-cost substitute. A play is needed, and it should be built around the failure history rather than the feature set: this prospect has quit at two weeks three times, and is currently at three weeks.

SECOND SCRIPT GAP — no low-cost entry rung. The prospect articulated the want precisely and reasonably: prove the interest cheaply, then commit capital. 'I would first go and buy a small, used bicycle... and then ride it a bit, and then see if I really like it, and then see if that's really a priority... and after a year, then I'll see if I'm prepared to spend 6k.' Nothing was offered between free content and $6,000 — no guide, no short trial, no single onboarding session, no deposit that holds a price. The rep went straight from $6,000 to third-party financing to goodbye. Whether the business wants a lower rung is a strategy decision, but the absence of one turned a motivated prospect into a clean loss with no residual relationship and nothing sent.

adherence.notes: Paradoxically one of the better-run calls in the batch and a correct outcome: the rep asked real why-questions, refused the 'I have no time' excuse and got to the truth ('I don't like it enough'), pre-empted a think-about-it, ran the most complete money play of the batch, and disqualified cleanly rather than discounting. Three things to coach. First, he ignored two clear stop signals — the prospect flatly rejecting the deep why ('It won't change my life') and pre-flagging the price ('Sounds expensive') — and pressed on to the number both times instead of returning to Phase 5, which the script tells him to do. Second, Phase 5 was never run at all, despite the prospect handing him the single best consequence image in the corpus: a 75-year-old father who looks 95 and cannot get up. Third, and most fixable, he conceded the not-the-right-time objection instead of quoting the prospect's own words back at him from thirty-five minutes earlier. Above the rep's head: this lead should never have reached a closer. He came from an Instagram ad he had not sought, did not know what the call was, had zero liquid cash, and measured fitness spending against a $25 tub of protein. That is a qualification failure upstream, and it cost forty-three minutes of closing time.

objections.rep_response: Agreed with the premise rather than fighting it, then converted it into the accountability case: 'Of course, Trevor is the best in this space when it comes to kettlebells, but it's going to be you that's going to be doing the work. He can coach you, he can keep you accountable, but you have to show up every day.' He followed with a motivation argument built on the prospect's children. Well handled, but the prospect did not visibly move on — he changed the subject to his blood pressure.

evidence: The recording is truncated. It ends mid-sentence at 00:18:24, in the middle of the rep's opening line of the consequence frame — 'Look, I'm going to be brutally honest with you. You're 39... We're not getting any younger, you're 105 kilos, the lifestyle that you're living right now, the amount of stress that you have, and the...' — with the prospect's reply 'Very heavy.' and then nothing.

No pillars were presented, no delivery walkthrough, no tiers, no price, no commitment check and no close attempt appear anywhere in the recorded portion. The outcome is not merely unclear, it is absent from the artifact.

Undetermined is used deliberately rather than follow_up: there is no evidence a follow-up was discussed, and equally no evidence the call ended here. The 16 KB file size and the clean mid-sentence cut point to a recording or export failure rather than a short call.

Directional signals up to the cut, for whoever picks this up: intent was high and already acted upon — he had bought two kettlebells, started training, cut bread, sugar, sodas and fast food two weeks earlier, and stated 'I decided so it needs to be changed.' He was also already asking to buy instruction: 'that's why I was thinking about maybe to get the proper lesson, of course. Let's see how we can manage it.'

Counter-evidence: he pre-emptively pushed back on the value of external coaching — 'the change, it will not come, definitely not come from you. It will come from me' — and no money conversation had begun, so affordability is entirely unknown.

notable.note: Two things. First, a data-integrity problem: this transcript is truncated at 00:18:24, mid-sentence, with no ending. The disposition is unrecoverable from this artifact and the file should be re-pulled from Fathom or checked for a second part before this call is counted in any rep or funnel statistic. Second, and the reason this call is worth recovering: it is the clearest clinical-risk case in the batch and simultaneously the strongest sales setup. The prospect is 39, 105 kg, with a spinal disc compression diagnosed three years ago, a right knee that subluxes ('it might be hopping out'), a hip that will not let him cross one leg, and high blood pressure — and he has spent the last two weeks doing unsupervised kettlebell work from Trevor's free videos and has developed new back pain as a result. He half-diagnosed it himself: 'Maybe I do something wrong.' That is the single best argument for paid coaching anywhere in this batch and also the single loudest signal that a clinical screen is needed before selling loaded ballistic training. Nothing in the recorded portion asks whether any clinician has cleared him. On the positive side, this is the only call in the batch where the rep demonstrably used the application ('I saw in the application that you run your own company') and the only one with a genuinely thorough baseline — age, height, weight, occupation, sitting percentage, injuries with duration, diet, energy and working hours were all asked directly. One coaching note visible even in the fragment: the prospect reported sleeping about six hours and the rep replied 'Okay. Not bad.' For a hypertensive 39-year-old with self-identified cortisol-driven fat gain, six hours is a finding, not a pass.

quality.notes: Frequent inversion, plus a truncated recording. Roles read from content throughout. Clear misattributions: at 00:00:55 the frame ('These calls are very simple. I just want to understand...') sits under the prospect's label but is the rep; at 00:09:22-00:10:11 the steroid explanation and the line 'the muscles grow faster than your joints can adapt' are split across labels with the rep's coaching point landing under the prospect; at 00:13:15-00:13:17 the exchange about children is fully inverted, so 'Do you have kids?' appears under the prospect and 'Yeah, I have two daughters' appears under the rep — the daughters are the prospect's, confirmed by his later line 'I cannot keep, I think I'm too fat for that.' Audio quality was poor at the start: the prospect's laptop produced heavy noise and he switched to headphones around 00:01:19, and roughly the first two minutes are consumed by technical issues. The recording then stops mid-sentence at 00:18:24 with no closing. The rep's display label reads 'Andrew Jin (Primal Instinct)' while the title and folder say Andrew Musial; recorded as Andrew Musial, flagged for confirmation.

P1.evidence: P1a partial, and the best P1a in the batch — the rep had demonstrably read the application and used it: 'And I saw in the application that you run your own company, correct?' It scores partial rather than hit because it was one fact deployed mid-baseline as a question, not a read-back at the open designed to make the prospect feel seen. P1b partial: three of the four parts — 'I just want to understand. What's going on? What have you tried? And where are you trying to get to?' — with 'what you need' again absent. P1c hit: 'Sounds good?' asked and answered, 'Yeah, of course.' P1d hit: 'walk me through, like, what's been going on? Like, what's the main thing you're looking to fix right now?', and he re-asked it verbatim after the audio problems were resolved rather than letting it drop.

P2.evidence: Comfortably the strongest baseline in the batch and the only one with no outright misses. P2a hit — all three asked directly and in sequence: 'how old you right now?', 'roughly how tall are you?', 'what's your weight currently?' P2b hit, and the best execution of this check anywhere in the batch: he opened from the application, then tested the nature of the work ('Management work? Sitting in front of the desk?'), then quantified it rather than accepting a vague answer — 'if you would say, percentage-wise, 50% of the day you spent in front of the desk or more?' — which produced 70% seated. P2c partial: 'Any other chronic conditions and anything?' was asked, but hereditary history was never raised and the high blood pressure surfaced later, volunteered rather than elicited. P2d hit and thorough: 'Do you have like any injuries or anything that is limiting your movement right now?', then refusing the vague answer with 'What do you mean, not so good?', then establishing the ten-year duration, then probing a specific region on a hypothesis — 'How about the hips? Like do you feel...' — which uncovered the one-sided restriction. P2e partial: 'did you, like before that, did you do any workouts? Did you go to the gym?' produced the steroid history and the current two-week block, but he never established how many days a week the prospect actually trains now. P2f partial: never asked as a results question, though the most important result — new back pain from self-taught kettlebell work — was uncovered by 'Does it result, like, do you have back pains also?' P2g hit: 'in terms of nutrition, like how do you eat right now?', then 'any particular diet?', then the useful compliance probe 'what's your favorite food?' which produced 'if anything is sweet, it's my favorite food'. P2h partial: sleep was never asked directly and never probed for quality; it fell out of the working-hours question, and when the answer came back as roughly six hours the rep replied 'Okay. Not bad.' For a hypertensive 39-year-old who has just attributed his own fat gain to cortisol, six hours is a finding to work, not a pass. P2i hit: 'how do you feel, like, on a day-to-day, like, with energy and everything?' produced the crashes, the supplements and the stress.

P3.evidence: P3a hit: 'if you would have one goal that you would like to achieve right now, like, what would it be? Like, what's the focus right now?' P3b miss — the mobility/strength/energy menu was never offered. P3c hit, and the best-placed question on the call: 'Do you sometimes ran out of breath when she's running around?' produced the emotional centre of the whole conversation — 'sometimes they like to run out, but I cannot keep, I cannot, I think I'm too fat for that.' P3d, P3e, P3f and P3g all partial for the same recurring reason: the rep found the right territory and then supplied the meaning himself instead of asking for it. He asked 'do you have kids?' as a fact-finder and then delivered the significance as a monologue — 'guys who have kids... they tend to perform better. Because that's the biggest driver for them, that you want to be there healthy... you want to play with them.' Likewise on the goal he asserted the consequence and asked only for confirmation: 'imagine that you would actually lose this excessive weight, I don't know, 10, 15 kilos, that would probably allow you to do that, yeah?' The prospect had just handed him 'I'm too fat to keep up with my daughters' and the correct next move was silence and 'what does that feel like?', not a paragraph. Telling is that the prospect then redirected the conversation himself, to his blood pressure. P3h not_applicable — the reflect-back had not yet been reached when the recording stopped; the phase was still in progress.

P4.evidence: P4a hit — asked in the frame and then pursued directly with 'did you, like before that, did you do any workouts? Did you go to the gym?', which produced the year of steroid-assisted heavy training. P4b hit and asked cleanly: 'So, what happened? Like, why this excessive weight? What happened?' P4c partial — the cause was pursued, but the rep supplied the hypothesis rather than letting the prospect reach it: 'is it connected, like the stress levels that you have in your work, and you probably tend to eat more when you're stressed?' A leading question that happened to be right. P4d partial — the stress-eating loop was identified but never framed as the one thing in the way. P4e partial — the prospect did name his own gap, and named it well ('I'm struggling to not do that... one half of your body says, come, let's eat something more'), but he was walked there rather than getting there. P4f miss, and it is the most expensive omission in the recorded portion. The scripted line is 'the information isn't the problem — why can't you stick to it on your own?', and this prospect had spent two weeks proving the answer: he had Trevor's free videos, bought the kettlebells, started on his own, and given himself back pain. 'Maybe I do something wrong' was an open invitation and the rep acknowledged it warmly ('It's good to start, you know. That's the first step') instead of using it. The phase was still live when the recording cut, so this may have been run afterwards — but it was not run at the moment it was handed to him.

P5.evidence: The consequence frame was demonstrably being initiated at the exact moment the recording ends. P5a partial: 'Look, I'm going to be brutally honest with you. You're 39... We're not getting any younger, you're 105 kilos, the lifestyle that you're living right now, the amount of stress that you have, and the...' — the prospect answered 'Very heavy.' and the file stops mid-sentence. The move was started and its content is unobservable, so it is scored partial rather than credited or penalised. P5b, P5c and P5d are not_applicable because the recording, not the call, ended before them. Whoever re-pulls this file should re-score the phase: on the evidence of the opening line the rep was running Phase 5 properly and in the right order, before any presentation, which is more than can be said for the other closer calls in this batch.

P6.evidence: Not reached in the recorded portion — the transcript ends inside Phase 5. Scored N/A because the artifact is truncated, not because the rep skipped it; no inference either way is available.

P11.evidence: No offer, no price and no close attempt appear anywhere in the recorded portion, so the payment and onboarding sequence was never reachable within the artifact.

objection_plays.detail: A self-reliance objection with no scripted play: 'the change, it will not come, definitely not come from you. It will come from me. You can say whatever you want if I don't do it.' None of the five plays map — it is not money, timing, a spouse, a delay or fear; it is a prospect pre-emptively discounting the value of any coach. The rep handled it about as well as improvisation allows, conceding the true part and converting it into the accountability argument: 'Trevor is the best in this space when it comes to kettlebells, but it's going to be you that's going to be doing the work. He can coach you, he can keep you accountable, but you have to show up every day.' Scored partial rather than hit because the prospect did not visibly move on — he changed the subject to his blood pressure — and because the rep followed with a generic motivation monologue about men with children rather than tying accountability back to the specific evidence sitting in front of him, which was two weeks of unsupervised training that had just injured the man's back. Worth building a play for: this objection will recur with self-made business owners.

adherence.notes: Score this one as provisional — the transcript is truncated at 00:18:24 and Phases 5 through 11 are unobservable, so the phase weights that matter most for outcome are missing. On what is visible, this is the best-executed front half in the batch: the only genuine use of the application, and by a distance the most thorough baseline, including the two questions the rep skips everywhere else — occupation with a quantified sitting percentage, and injuries pursued past the first vague answer. Two coaching points are already visible. First, he consistently finds the emotional territory and then talks over it; when the prospect said 'I'm too fat to keep up with my daughters' the correct move was a question and a silence, and what followed was a monologue about how men with kids perform better, after which the prospect changed the subject. Second, he let the single strongest piece of evidence on the call go by: this man is currently self-coaching from Trevor's free videos and has hurt his back doing it, which is Phase 4's 'why can't you stick to it on your own' answering itself, and the rep replied 'It's good to start.' Above the coaching: the clinical picture here — diagnosed disc compression, a subluxing knee, a locked hip, hypertension at 105 kg, and a fresh training injury — needs a clearance question that the playbook does not contain, and re-pulling the full recording should be treated as a prerequisite to any decision about this prospect.

Like, I just want to buy a program' — and he explicitly rejected the accountability pillar, which is a third of the offer. Getting him onto a 30-day trial does not resolve that; it defers it by a month.
outcome.next_step: Follow-up call Friday at 1pm Pacific; rep to send the calendar invite by email. Jared to 'look at a few other things' and confirm whether he wants the $1,500 30-day trial, possibly the same day.

notable.note: The most serious pricing finding in the batch. Over roughly four minutes the rep walked the price down three times in response to nothing but hesitation: $6,000 for six months, then $4,000 for three months, then an invented $1,500 for 30 days branded 'love it or leave it'. The three-month tier at $4,000 is not in the documented offer and this is the second time the same rep has quoted it in three days. The 30-day trial appears to have been created on the call — the rep proposed it himself ('Can I propose something? Would you be down for, like, 30 days just checking how it works?') with no refund terms, no mechanics and, judging by the internal onboarding call recorded the day before, no authorisation. That call established the sanctioned payment structure as 50% today and 50% at 30 days, told this rep that longer splits are 'not generally an option that we offer', and then told him 'if you're on a call and you need to get creative, worst case, you try to make something work... if we need to get the deal through.' This call is what that licence produces. Three further flags. (1) The rep invited the prospect to reject a third of the offer before delivering it: 'And the third part, you said that you don't need hand-holding. Is that correct?' Jared duly said no, and the accountability pillar — the single most defensible reason to pay $6,000 — was dead before it was presented. (2) At the moment the prospect said the trial 'would work', the rep did not ask for payment. He explained the trial again and then agreed to a follow-up. (3) The rep twice in this batch has told a prospect 'you're not our typical client' — said here at 00:10:26, ten minutes in and before any pitch. Also worth capturing as reference data: this is the first call in the batch where the setter is identifiable, and the transcript confirms KL = Kyla, with the rep having genuinely read her notes before the call.

quality.notes: Pervasive inversion; roles read from content. Examples: at 00:01:46 'Any serious things?' is the rep's question but sits under his label immediately followed by Jared's answer in the same block; at 00:05:04 'Anything else that I need to know of?' sits under Jared but is the rep; at 00:09:40 'because you mentioned those shoulder injuries, do you have like stiffness in them?' sits under Jared but is plainly the rep; and at 00:14:24 'Second thing is nutrition' is split so the pillar heading lands under Jared and the body lands under the rep. The pricing exchange at 00:19:57-00:20:14 is the worst affected and the most consequential: '6K. 6K. 5K. 5K.' appears under the rep's label as apparent ASR noise or an echo, and the tier prices alternate across both labels. The 6K/6-month and 4K/3-month figures are recoverable with confidence from context; the stray '5K' is not treated as a quoted price. One further ambiguity recorded rather than resolved: at 00:18:12 the twelve-month tier is described as 'Just, I would recommend 12 months for you. It's too long. It's for the, like, beginners' — internally contradictory, and the rep then pitched six months, so recommended_tier_months is recorded as 6. Similarly at 00:23:31 'so for three months, that would be 1,500' appears where the context is unambiguously the 30-day trial, and is recorded as the 30-day price.

P1.evidence: P1a hit, and the only clean hit on this check in the batch — the rep signalled he had read the setter's notes and then proved it: 'So I went through everything that you told to my friend, Kaila. Yeah, there's a lot going on over there', followed by 'you have an experience of training twice a day, doing high rocks, all of stuff.' That is the check working as intended. P1b partial and thinner than his usual frame: 'I just want to understand where you're at right now and how we can actually potentially help you with', plus the takeaway, 'if there's an alignment, of course I can show you everything in granular. But if not, that's totally fine too.' Two of four parts — what you have tried and what you need were both absent. P1c partial: he tagged 'Yeah?' onto the frame and got 'Cool. Yeah', but never asked the explicit agreement question. P1d hit: 'brief me in your own words, like, what you're actually looking for.'

P2.evidence: Split down the middle: everything about training was asked well and everything about the person was skipped. P2a miss — no age, no height, no weight, on a fitness sale. P2b miss, and expensive: the rep learned the prospect travels constantly and has back-to-back meetings all day, asked where he was going (Mykonos, Ibiza, Saint-Tropez, Marbella) and never once asked what he does for a living. That is the ICP's occupation test, unasked, on the wealthiest prospect in the batch. P2c partial — injury questions were asked, but no general health or hereditary screen. P2d hit and well run: 'Any serious things?' produced the bilateral labral tears and stem cell treatment, 'Anything else that I need to know of?' produced the metal bar, eight screws and flat feet, and he followed up specifically — 'because you mentioned those shoulder injuries, do you have like stiffness in them?' Duration was not established, which is the only shortfall. P2e hit — the training week was mapped thoroughly: The Yard in the morning, gym in the afternoon, daily, plus 'Apart from gym, do you play any sports?' and 'do you have like a home gym, or do you have to come [to a gym]'. P2f hit — 'What's the biggest piece missing for you right now in terms of training that you do currently? Apart that you're bored with it' is exactly the results probe, and it produced the core and leg-day gaps. P2g hit — 'how about your diet? How does it look like? Is it dialed in or?', then the good follow-up 'is there an issue with that when you tend to fall off during travels?', which produced 'one bite turns into 20'. P2h and P2i miss — sleep and energy never raised, on a man training twice a day across time zones.

P3.evidence: The surface half ran and the deep half did not run at all, and that is the whole story of this call. P3a hit — 'Do you have, like, a specific goal with it that you want to achieve?' P3b hit and near-verbatim — 'if you would have to say like, would it be like getting stronger or like overall mobility type of thing?' produced mobility as the priority and core as the secondary. P3c partial — 'Any PRs that you want to hit?' is the nearest approach to something he wants and can't do; the answer was no and it was not pursued. P3d, P3e, P3f and P3g are all misses and there is no partial credit available: the bridge question was never asked in any form, no version of 'outside of the physical, what's actually driving this' appeared, nobody was ever asked what moving better would do for him, nobody was asked who else it impacts, and nothing was driven through to family, identity, legacy or longevity. The rep did not establish this man's age, occupation, or whether he has a partner or children. The entire conversation stayed on logistics: travel, equipment and boredom. P3h partial — there were reflect-backs, but only of surface facts: 'So basically, you're looking for something that you could implement into your workouts when you're traveling, right?' and 'So mobility would be the baseline for you and the foundation.' The consequence is direct and traceable: with nothing emotional ever attached to the purchase, the prospect's own summary of what he was buying became 'In my mind, what I want is just a program' — which is exactly what a call that never left the logistics layer produces.

P4.evidence: P4a partial — current training was mapped in detail but past attempts were never asked about; the Barry's-style classes surfaced on their own. P4b and P4c miss, and this is the costly pair. The prospect volunteered his own failure pattern in one sentence — 'eventually I just got so bored of it. I couldn't go anymore' — and he is currently sitting in the same pattern with a gym routine he is 'just over'. Boredom-driven abandonment is his root cause, it appeared twice unprompted, and the rep asked nothing about it either time. P4d partial — 'What's the biggest piece missing for you right now in terms of training that you do currently?' is a gap question, but it produced preferences (core, leg day) rather than structure. P4e miss — no structural gap was ever named. P4f miss, and it went beyond omission into self-harm: rather than asking why he cannot sustain this on his own, the rep asked him to confirm that he can — 'And the third part, you said that you don't need hand-holding. Is that correct?' The prospect agreed, and the accountability case was surrendered before it was made.

P5.evidence: Not run in any form. No cost of inaction, no two-year question, no settling question, no line in the sand. There was material available — a plateau he is frustrated by, four labral tears held together by stem cell injections, a rodded leg, and a documented history of quitting things from boredom — and none of it was turned into a consequence. Without Phase 5 the price had nothing to sit against, which is why the conversation moved straight from the number to a negotiation about scope.

P6.evidence: P6a miss — the belief question was never asked. P6b partial — two soft temperature checks stood in for it: 'So how do you feel about overall?' and 'So does it sound like you want to do it, or like, eh?' Neither is the scripted go-all-in question and neither surfaces hidden blockers. P6c miss, and clearly so. The answer to 'does it sound like you want to do it' was not a yes, it was a question — 'if I say yes, is it just like, I get a full program, or like, just curious how it works, and what the price is, I guess?' The rep proceeded to deliverables and then to the number anyway, and never returned to Phase 5 when the scope objection landed. He had also, minutes earlier, been told the accountability pillar was unwanted, which is the clearest possible signal to go back rather than forward.

P11.evidence: P11a is scored a miss rather than N/A because the moment became live and was not taken. After the rep proposed the 30-day trial, the prospect said 'Yeah, I think that would work', and after the rep confirmed the price the prospect said 'Okay, cool.' At that point payment should have been requested. Instead the rep re-explained the trial and accepted 'let me just check a few other things and then I will get back to you.' No card was asked for, no link was mentioned, and the deal was pushed to Friday. P11b, P11c and P11d are N/A: with no payment taken, the Trevor onboarding booking, the agreement signature and the welcome-email walkthrough were unreachable.

objection_plays.detail: Triggered twice. On the first ('I'll think on it. I'll let you guys know') the rep ran the single best move in the play and ran it well: 'So what's coming up for you right now that's keeping you from actually moving forward?' It worked — it produced a specific, actionable answer rather than a stall, 'I just don't know, for me personally, if me spending $4,000 on this makes sense.' He then stopped running the play and started building product instead. Not run at any point: 'do you feel what we've gone through CAN get you to [goal]', 'what makes you feel it can', 'thinking isn't the problem, deciding is', 'the way you've been approaching this brought you here — when do you make a different decision', 'that man you want to be, how does HE decide right now', and the closing 'are you sure? Nothing else keeping you from being 100% in?' On the second trigger, twenty seconds after the prospect had said the trial would work, the rep granted the delay outright with no play at all.

Recorded deliberately as a non-trigger, because it superficially looks like a money objection and is not. The prospect ruled money out himself, unprompted and emphatically: 'it's not even like the $4,000. I spend way more on stupid [stuff] all the time', against a disclosed baseline of the $1,000–$2,500 band-$2,000 a month on personal trainers. Running the open-wallet play here — asking for cash on hand, credit cards, available credit — would have been both wrong and insulting. The rep correctly did not run it, and that judgement deserves credit. The problem is what he ran instead: having correctly diagnosed that price was not the barrier, he responded by cutting the price three times.

SCRIPT GAP, and a new one — value at reduced scope. The prospect does not want the offer; he wants a third of it. 'I'd rather just pay for a program is really where my head's at, more so than paying for an ongoing handholding', and then plainly, 'what I want is not necessarily something that you guys normally sell. Like, I just want to buy a program.' None of the five plays addresses a prospect who accepts the value, can afford the price, and rejects the scope. The rep tried one rebuttal — that a kettlebell novice needs the coaching layer — and when the prospect conceded month one and refused the rest, the counter was a single line: 'Well, you will learn the basics throughout the month, and then you will progress, right?' He then stopped arguing and started discounting. Scored partial for the attempted rebuttal. A real play is needed here, and it should probably be built on the prospect's own failure pattern — this is a man who quits things when he gets bored, which is an argument for check-ins, not against them, and it was sitting in the transcript unused.

SECOND SCRIPT GAP — in-person versus virtual value. 'I spend 1,500, 2K a month sometimes on trainers when I'm here... to spend the same amount for virtual seems a little crazy.' The rep asked the right opening question, 'What's so crazy about it?', which is exactly how to attack an unexamined assumption, and then dropped it when the answer came back soft ('just a different experience in my mind'). No play exists for the modality objection, and it is the one that matters most for a premium remote offer sold to people who already buy in-person training. The unused counter was on the table: this prospect travels roughly half the year, and an in-person trainer in Los Angeles does not exist in Mykonos.

THIRD SCRIPT GAP — free online resources, the third appearance of this shape in this batch. 'For what I want, and all the online resources and things, like, it just seems silly for me to spend so much money on.' Unlike the other two occurrences, here it drew no response whatsoever; the rep said 'Okay. I get it' and pivoted to proposing the trial. Logging it because the frequency now matters: three of the four sales calls in this batch were partly or wholly lost to a free alternative, and the playbook has nothing for it.

adherence.notes: The clearest example in the batch of good front-of-call work being wasted by skipping the middle. Genuine strengths: the only real read-back of setter notes anywhere in this batch, thorough injury and training-history questioning, an accurate read that money was not the objection, and one well-run Objection A move that produced a specific blocker instead of a stall. Then everything that creates willingness to pay was skipped — the whole deep half of Phase 3, all of Phase 4's root cause, all of Phase 5, and any real commitment check — so when the number landed there was nothing holding it up. Two moments to coach specifically. First, at 00:14:26 the rep asked the prospect to confirm he did not need the accountability pillar before presenting it; that single question surrendered a third of the offer and became the prospect's central objection six minutes later. Second, on being told the scope was wrong, the rep cut price three times in four minutes — $6,000, then $4,000, then an invented $1,500 30-day trial he named 'love it or leave it' on the spot — and then, when the prospect agreed to the trial, did not ask for payment. Escalate the pricing separately from the coaching: the $4,000 three-month tier is not in the documented offer and this rep has now quoted it twice in three days, and the 30-day trial appears to have been created live with no terms, one day after his manager told him longer or non-standard payment structures are 'not generally an option that we offer' while also telling him to get creative if he needed to get a deal through.

The rep then re-establishes the whole baseline from call one before proceeding. Together the two files are a single conversation of roughly 64 minutes.

objections.raw_quote: You know, to be honest, 9K is not a small amount, even if we know we have good salaries here in Denmark. But either how, 9K is a lot of money, to be honest. It's not like a small amount, because it is a big amount. Even for Denmark, we have a good salary and we have a good lifestyle, but...

Is there anything else apart from money that could be stopping you?' Got a clean isolation — 'It's nothing else that can stop me.' Then asked 'what's coming up?', then opened the payment door and stepped down to the six-month tier at $6,000 with a discounted $3,000 renewal for months seven to twelve.

Of course, it's about my health, but maybe it is, it doesn't, it might be, sounds stupid. The cheaper version, but let's see what other alternatives we have to this.
objections.rep_response: Did not answer immediately — he isolated first and asked what was coming up, which was correct sequencing. He then presented the six-month tier at $6,000, the the the $500–$1,000 band+ band renewal top-up, and three payment structures. The prospect chose six months paid monthly.

Either I choose you, and I go with you for a certain amount, even if I find another chance or somebody else, it's like a way, in a way or another, I will do it. Either with you, either with somebody else.

The prospect had just said out loud that he views Primal as interchangeable with an unnamed competitor, and nothing was done to differentiate.

So it's like, you know, I have to be certain about some things... I will run a process. I will check a little bit your background and Trevor's and like this.

The prospect rejected the frame firmly and reasonably. The rep then asked what information was needed rather than having anything ready to send, ran a good conditional close ('if I would send you this information today or tomorrow and everything checks out, you ready to move forward?' — answered yes), and then asked for a $100 refundable deposit, which the prospect refused.
