objections.raw_quote: I was not aware it was going to be that much, in which case now I feel terrible for taking up your time. I can't do either of them.
objections.rep_response: Did not react to the surprise itself. He moved straight to isolation — 'just to make sure, finances side, because we can talk about numbers, are you, like, you feel confident that you actually can get to your goals with this?' — which was the right sequencing, but the fact that a prospect reached the price after fifty minutes with no idea of the order of magnitude was never acknowledged or escalated.

objections.raw_quote: I, the financial is where it's going to stop. Like, that is, I have no ability to change that at this point in time.
objections.rep_response: Ran Objection C properly and to conclusion. Isolated twice, reframed to should-versus-how ('you're not in a, let's say, should place, but, like, how to do it?'), opened the payment door, asked permission for an open financial conversation, and then took the picture: cash on hand (the under $500 band), how he lives on it, and credit cards ('Could, but I'm paying that off right now'). Having established the position he stopped rather than grinding, and pivoted to sending free materials.

objections.raw_quote: Currently paying back my retirement for an issue that I had in the house. And I've got my mortgage. So there's not much wiggle room. And the retirement will be paid off in two years. And then I've got the credit card. So I don't have a specific time for it.
objections.rep_response: Asked the right question — 'how do you feel when you said that you're gonna pay that off? Like, what's the timeframe?' — got a two-year horizon with no defined end for the credit card, and correctly did not push against it. He closed with 'I'll send you some materials that you can start working by yourself... and we can have another conversation in some time. I'm not giving up on you.'

objections.raw_quote: How about when I get to the financial point that I can do this? I did get Trevor's free follow along guide. And once it's paid off, I'll reach back out to y'all. I have no problems with doing a little bit here and there. And then when I get to the point where I can pay the money, I'll reach back out to y'all. Because I understand that you still have to make money yourself, so no worries there.
objections.rep_response: Answered the apology rather than the substance, and did it well: 'Look, it's not about me. My life won't change if you're gonna buy or if you're not gonna buy. My life won't change. But yours, definitely, this is a life-changing moment.' He then agreed to the prospect's own proposal and extended it by offering to send further materials. Proposed label for this objection type: self_directed_interim_plan — a prospect proposing to use the free product until he can afford the paid one.

offer.payment_plan_terms: No structure was ever named. The rep said only 'Most of the clients just take it upfront, but for some of them, it shouldn't be the way that they should proceed. I understand that. So we don't have any set payment plans. It's all customized depending on what's best for the client.' The financial picture that followed established there was nothing to structure. Note this is the same 'no set payment plans' formulation the rep used with Bruno on 25 May, and it contradicts both the structured plans he quoted to Marian S. and João D. and the policy stated on the internal onboarding call.

evidence: Explicit and immediate refusal of both tiers on first hearing the price: 'I was not aware it was going to be that much, in which case now I feel terrible for taking up your time. I can't do either of them.'
Confirmed as absolute rather than negotiable when isolated: 'the financial is where it's going to stop. Like, that is, I have no ability to change that at this point in time.'

The financial picture the rep then took confirms it independently: the under $500 band of cash on hand, credit cards being paid down, a retirement loan with a two-year repayment horizon, and a mortgage.

No payment, no payment link, no verbal agreement, and no follow-up call was scheduled — only an open-ended intention: 'we can have another conversation in some time' and 'I'm not giving up on you... give me a few days and I will send you the materials.'

Counter-evidence, and it is why the confidence is 0.9 rather than higher: intent and belief were both fully established before the number. He confirmed 'yes' to the belief check, took personal responsibility unprompted ('Because I'm the only one that can help me'), and granted the rep permission to hold him accountable. He also proposed re-contacting Primal himself once his debts clear. This is a relationship that could reopen, but not on any timeline either party could name.
The prospect's own timeline for affordability was two years for the retirement loan and undefined for the credit card, so treating this as a follow_up would overstate it.
outcome.next_step: No call scheduled. The rep committed to sending free training materials within a few days and to staying in touch; the prospect committed to reaching back out when his debts are cleared. Nothing dated on either side.

notable.note: The best-executed process in the batch, run on a prospect who could never have bought, and the two facts together are the finding. PROCESS: this is the only call in the batch where the consequence frame, the commitment check and the money play all ran properly, and the money play is the textbook run — isolate, should-versus-how, permission, then cash on hand and credit — after which the rep stopped rather than grinding a man with the under $500 band to his name. He then did something not in the playbook and worth recording: he sent the prospect away with free materials and 'I'm not giving up on you', having first refused the prospect's apology with 'it's not about me. My life won't change if you're gonna buy or if you're not gonna buy.' QUALIFICATION FAILURE: the prospect gave three explicit financial warnings before the pitch — 'money's a little tight, so there is more carbs than I should be, just because it's cheaper' at 00:07:39, 'a good amount of it right now has been due to my financial instability... just bought a house and then there was a bunch of issues with it' at 00:17:09, and, in direct answer to the go-all-in question at 00:31:12, 'Other than I'm curious on the financial side of it.' All three were passed over, and fifty minutes of closing time went into a $6,000 presentation for someone with the under $500 band. He also arrived with no price expectation at all, from an Instagram ad, not knowing who Trevor was: 'not at all actually.' CLINICAL: Ehlers-Danlos syndrome is a genetic connective tissue disorder and this prospect subluxes a shoulder catching a door and a kneecap while walking. He is under chiropractic and physiotherapy care, and the rep — uniquely in this batch — actually asked about clinicians and about compliance with prescribed exercises. He then never asked whether either clinician would sanction loaded ballistic kettlebell work, and pitched it as the answer. Of every prospect in this batch this is the one where the missing clinical screen carries the most physical risk. NUTRITION: the pillar prescribed meat, eggs, vegetables and fruit to a man who had already said he eats cheap carbohydrates because money is tight. The cost of the prescribed diet was never addressed. ICP: he is very close to the literal negative example in Primal's own stated ICP — 'dudes who come here who are 50 pounds overweight, who are just like, I need to just lose weight and I hate working out' — and he still received a full closer call.

quality.notes: Severe, and worse at both ends of the call than in the middle. The entire opening through 00:01:02 is a single undifferentiated block under the rep's label containing both the rep's frame and the prospect's first answer about EDS. The closing from roughly 00:53:41 to 00:55:01 collapses the same way, merging the rep's nurture offer with the prospect's replies. Individual inversions throughout: at 00:09:56 'How get back to this?' is split across labels mid-question; at 00:11:55 'And when you say feel comfortable, like' sits under the prospect but is the rep; at 00:16:44 the rep's own recap 'I think 15 years ago was the last time that you weighed like 180' lands under the prospect; and at 00:47:26 'Which direction feels better for you?' sits under the prospect but is plainly the rep, immediately before the prospect's 'You said six D, like six zero?' The pricing is nonetheless unambiguous from context — $6,000 for six months and $9,000 for twelve, confirmed by the rep's clarification 'For six months, it's $6K, $6,000.' The prospect's connection dropped several times, which he flagged himself ('my apologies if it cuts in and out. Apparently, my internet is acting funny'), and there are several passages of ASR noise ('talking almost thesis', 'my AED meds were awesome' for ADD meds, 'the counter-tractor' for chiropractor). The rep again carries the 'Andrew Jin (Primal Instinct)' label.

P1.evidence: P1a miss — nothing from an application or setter notes was read back, and no setter is referenced anywhere on the call. P1b partial, the standard three of four: 'these calls are very simple, I just want to understand what's going on, what have you tried, where are you trying to get to, and if there's an alignment we can talk about it, if not that's fine too, we just shake hands and part as friends.' What you need was again unframed. P1c hit — 'sounds good' asked and agreed. P1d partial: instead of the scripted open question the rep asked a context question, 'tell me how well do you know Trevor and his work, the kettlebell training?' It functioned well — the answer produced the Ehlers-Danlos disclosure inside forty seconds — but it is a source question, not an invitation to state what they want help with.

P2.evidence: The strongest baseline in the batch. P2a hit — 'roughly where are you at in terms of your weight and your height?' and 'how old are you?', and when the weight answer came back vague ('technically obese') he returned to it later and got 220 lb. P2b hit — occupation, the seven baseball fields, and crucially whether the work is sedentary: 'You move around a lot?' produced five to ten miles of walking a day, and later the full 3am-to-3.30pm schedule with commute. P2c hit — asked directly: 'apart from those injuries that you mentioned, do you have any like chronic conditions or anything like that?' P2d hit and by a distance the best injury questioning in the batch. He did not stop at the first answer on anything: 'How does that show up with the hips? Is it stiff or what's going on?', then 'what's going on with your lower back? Is it like pain?', then 'what's going on with the knees?', then 'is it like on a daily basis, like you feel it when you walk?' And uniquely in this batch he asked about clinical involvement and compliance: 'did you went to a doctor or like physiotherapist?', 'Did they assign you like with some workout regimen?', 'Did you follow that?', 'Are you doing that still?' — producing 'Should be, but no.' P2e hit — current training, home versus gym, and prior gym history all established. P2f partial — results from current training were not asked as such, though the physiotherapy-adherence line covered adjacent ground. P2g hit — nutrition asked, then 'And vegetables?', then the sweet tooth and alcohol frequency chased down. P2h miss, and it is the most conspicuous miss in the batch: this man wakes at 3am, drives, works a physical job until 2.30pm, drives 30 to 50 minutes home, and said in as many words 'I'm just tired, man.' Sleep quantity and quality were never asked. P2i hit — 'does that in any way affect you on a day-to-day? Like your work, your energy?', which produced the twelve-acre spraying story and the ice packs.

P3.evidence: P3a hit — 'if you would have to say, stated in your own words, what would be your main goal? Let's put it like in six months time, where would you like to be?' and he then quantified it properly, pushing past 'core muscles' to a waist size, a bodyweight and a date last held. P3b partial — the scripted mobility/strength/energy menu was never offered; instead he built his own forced choice between comfort and pain, which worked but is a different move. P3c hit, and it produced the best material on the call: asking what would change if the pain went produced archery, and he then tested it — 'Are you able to do that right now?' — surfacing that he manages about two quivers before his shooting degrades. P3d hit, run several times: 'Why is that more important than not feeling good on the beach?', 'how long have you actually been thinking about changing your situation, your health?', and 'Was there any particular moment that made you make this move? That you thought enough is enough?' P3e hit — 'if you think about what would actually change for you if you actually take care of this... how would you operate differently?' P3f miss — who else this impacts was never asked, and as a result nothing at all is known about whether this prospect has a partner or children. P3g partial — identity and ageing came through strongly ('I feel like I'm probably 10 years older than what I should be, comparative to my friends') and the rep future-paced six to eight months out, but family, marriage and legacy were never touched. P3h hit and textbook: 'from what I'm seeing, it's not only about feeling comfortable on the beach, but it's also about actually going through the day without pain. Would that be accurate?' — answered 'Yes, sir.'

P4.evidence: The third clean sweep of this phase by this rep in four days, and the best executed. P4a hit — 'Have you tried anything, actually, to get in better shape?' P4b hit — the outcomes were elicited in detail: the massage therapist moved away, the chiropractor 'would feel good for about a day, day or so, and then the pain would be back', the physiotherapist's exercises stopped. P4c hit — 'what do you feel like has actually been stopping you from fixing this up to this point?' P4d hit, and this is the standout moment of the call: the prospect gave the standard non-answer, 'Probably motivation, if I'm being honest', and the rep refused it — 'motivation is like, it's an emotion, it comes. It doesn't stick for a longer time. One day you're motivated, another day you're not. So, like, what's been really going on?' That produced the real obstacle: 'I would say motivation, but also, I'm just tired, man. I get up at 3.' P4e hit — the prospect named his own gap unprompted and precisely: 'everybody has the internet, so you have all the opportunity, right, but I lack the understanding and the system to go towards, because there's so many options that you can go with.' P4f hit — the substance of the information-isn't-the-problem move was achieved by that same line, elicited by the rep's persistence rather than handed over.

P5.evidence: The best consequence frame in the batch, and the only one where the rep had to fight for it. P5a hit, verbatim: 'Have you thought about what would it be if actually nothing changes, like in two years, five years, how it's going to be?' P5b hit, and this is the phase working properly under resistance. The prospect minimised — 'It's not going to be terrible if I weren't to change' — and the rep did not accept it. He came back with 'So do you think it's going to be the same or it's going to be worse?', got 'Probably worse', then used the prospect's own evidence against the minimisation: 'You got an issue from just holding a door.' Then he asked a third time: 'let me ask you again, do you really think that it's not going to be that bad in two years, three years, if you're not going to actually do something about it?' The answer changed to 'It won't be good. I'll tell you that much.' Three attempts to move a prospect off a comfortable answer is exactly what this check is for. P5c partial — 'why not' was never asked as a question; the rep asserted it instead ('I can only assume that staying at this current level is not acceptable to you') and got the answer anyway. P5d hit, in the strongest variant anywhere in this batch. Rather than the scripted line-in-the-sand phrasing he ran an ownership sequence: 'whose responsibility actually is it to make a change?' / 'Mine.' / 'Why so?' / 'Because I'm the only one that can help me.' He then pre-framed resistance ('we are masters of self-sabotage'), ran the devil-and-angel exercise to surface the self-sabotaging voice verbatim ('just another one of these. Let's see how long this one lasts'), had the prospect choose which voice to listen to and say why, and closed with a mandate: 'do I have your permission to hold you accountable, to hold you to the fire?' / 'Yeah.' / 'You sure? Because you know I will.'

P6.evidence: P6a hit, and correctly placed after the pillars and before the number: 'just to make sure we are on the same page, if you had the right training, simple nutrition, and real accountability, all built around your life, would you agree that you would get to your dream physique, and especially that you're going to be pain-free?' — answered 'Yes.' P6b hit and run early, before any presentation, at 00:31:03: 'is there anything outside yourself that would stop you from committing to this fully?' It was then re-run before pricing: 'if we can figure out the details, talk about the numbers, but are you fully actually committed to showing up and doing the work to become the better version of Alex?' — 'Yes.' P6c partial, and this is where the call went wrong, though not in the way the check usually fails. The yes was clear and correctly obtained. The problem is that the answer to P6b contained a warning the rep did not act on: 'Other than I'm curious on the financial side of it. And then, no.' The script's own instruction is to move forward only once you have a clear yes, and this was a conditional one. It was also the third financial signal of the call, after 'money's a little tight, so there is more carbs than I should be, just because it's cheaper' at 00:07:39 and 'a good amount of it right now has been due to my financial instability' at 00:17:09. Three flags, none qualified, and sixteen more minutes of building toward a $6,000 number.

P11.evidence: Both tiers were priced and a recommendation was made, but the prospect refused immediately and absolutely, so payment collection, the Trevor onboarding booking, the agreement signature and the welcome sequence were never reachable. Scored N/A so the phase does not double-penalise a refusal that no execution could have converted.

objection_plays.detail: The textbook run of this play in the batch, and the only one that scores a hit. ISOLATE FIRST ran twice, because the first attempt was deflected: 'just to make sure, finances side, are you, like, you feel confident that you actually can get to your goals with this?' got a restatement of the money problem, so he re-asked more precisely — 'What I'm asking is, are you 100% confident on the program itself, how it's structured, and that you actually can get to your goals?' — and got a clean 'Yes.' The should-versus-how move followed almost verbatim: 'you're not in a, let's say, should place, but, like, how to do it?' — 'Correct.' He confirmed the isolation a third time ('it's just a matter of working out the financials. Am I correct?') and even checked the self-sabotage voice was quiet ('So there's no devil screaming anything right now?'). He opened the payment door, then asked permission in the scripted form: 'are you comfortable having like an open and honest conversation about exactly where you're financially at right now?' Then the financial picture: cash on hand ('What's your cash on hand right now?' — the under $500 band), a probe into how that is possible, and credit cards ('do you have any credit cards that you could use?' — 'Could, but I'm paying that off right now'). Monthly surplus, number of cards, available credit and investments were not asked, and scoring this a hit rather than a partial is deliberate: the play's purpose is to establish whether the money can be found, that was established beyond doubt, and continuing to itemise a man with the under $500 band for gas would have been extractive rather than diligent. Stopping was the correct execution.

Triggered by the prospect's own deferral — 'when I get to the financial point that I can do this... once it's paid off, I'll reach back out to y'all.' The rep ran the play's core question, which is the one that matters: 'how do you feel when you said that you're gonna pay that off? Like, what's the timeframe?' The answer was two years for the retirement loan and no defined date for the credit card. None of the pressure moves ran — no 'things never slow down', no 'the longer you wait the harder this gets', no 'the only thing you can control is right now'. Scored partial, and the omission is defensible: the prospect's constraint is arithmetic, not psychology, and applying urgency to it would have been the wrong call. What is worth noting is that the rep had earned the right to use those lines — he had just established, over three attempts, that the joint problems will be worse in two years — and chose not to.

Run pre-emptively and to full effect, before the price, as inoculation rather than rebuttal. The rep pre-framed resistance — 'with anything that we change in life, there is always some level of resistance. We are masters of self-sabotage. Our brains are just basically wired to keep us safe and comfortable' — then asked for the accountability mandate and, when the answer was hedged ('I want to say yes'), pursued it: 'What makes you not saying that?' / 'Myself. Knowing myself.' He then externalised the doubt with the devil-and-angel exercise and got the self-sabotaging script quoted verbatim: 'just another one of these. Let's see how long this one lasts.' He had the prospect identify which voice the future version of himself needs to listen to, commit to it, and say why it was different this time — producing 'tired of feeling, tired of feeling' and 'having somebody that's keeping me accountable is a huge step in the right direction.' That is Objection E used before the objection exists, which is the strongest possible application, and it is the single best-run sequence in this batch.

SCRIPT AND PROCESS GAP — no price pre-frame anywhere upstream. 'I was not aware it was going to be that much, in which case now I feel terrible for taking up your time.' This prospect came from an Instagram advertisement, did not know who Trevor was ('not at all actually'), and reached minute forty-seven with no idea of the order of magnitude. There is no play for this because it is not a rep problem: it is a qualification and setting problem, and it is the second occurrence in this batch after Jorge Fernández, who arrived saying 'I don't know why I'm on this call.' Both were ad-sourced, both had no money, and both consumed most of an hour of closing time. A budget or price-band question at the setting stage would have caught both.

SCRIPT GAP — clinical fit, and the most physically serious instance in the batch. Ehlers-Danlos syndrome is a genetic connective tissue disorder; this prospect partially dislocated a shoulder catching a swinging door and subluxes a kneecap while walking. He is under the care of both a chiropractor and a physical therapist. The rep did better than anyone else in this batch on the front half of this — he is the only one who asked whether clinicians were involved and whether prescribed exercises were being followed — and then never asked the one question that matters: whether either clinician would sanction loaded ballistic kettlebell work for a hypermobility disorder. Instead the training pillar was presented as the answer to exactly those symptoms. The known gap in the playbook covers a clinician ruling the movement library out; here there is no mechanism to even consult one, and the prospect would not have known to ask.

SCRIPT GAP — cost-constrained nutrition. The prospect disclosed at 00:07:39 that he eats more carbohydrate than he wants because it is cheaper, and mentioned that he schedules groceries out. Thirty-two minutes later the nutrition pillar prescribed whole foods, eggs, meat, chicken, vegetables and fruit, with no reference to cost at all. There is no play, and no version of the pillar, for a prospect whose binding nutrition constraint is a grocery budget rather than knowledge or discipline. The rep engaged the sweet tooth by name and left the affordability of the prescription entirely unaddressed.

adherence.notes: The best-run call in this batch and a correct loss, which makes it the clearest evidence that process quality and outcome are separable here. Four phases scored hits — the baseline, goals, root cause and, uniquely, the consequence frame — and the commitment check and money play both ran properly and in the right order. Specific things worth extracting for coaching: refusing 'probably motivation' as an answer and getting 'I'm just tired, man, I get up at 3'; asking three times, against resistance, whether the joints will really be fine in two years, and using the prospect's own door incident to break the minimisation; the ownership sequence ending in 'because I'm the only one that can help me'; and the devil-and-angel exercise that had the prospect voice his own quitting script out loud before it could be used on him. The money play is the reference run: isolate, re-isolate when deflected, should-versus-how, permission, then cash and credit — and then stop, because the answer was the under $500 band. He also closed better than the situation deserved, refusing the prospect's apology with 'it's not about me, my life won't change if you're gonna buy or not' and sending him away with free materials. The failure is upstream and it is a qualification failure, not an execution one. Three explicit financial warnings were given before the pitch — cheap carbohydrates at 00:07, 'financial instability' at 00:17, and, in direct answer to the go-all-in question at 00:31, 'other than I'm curious on the financial side of it' — and all three were passed over. Fifty minutes of closing time went into a $6,000 presentation for a man with the under $500 band of cash. Escalate two things above the rep: an ad-sourced lead with no price expectation reaching a closer for the second time in this batch, and the absence of any clinical screen on a prospect with a genetic connective tissue disorder who dislocates joints opening doors.

source.display_title: 05/28/2026 - João D. x Andrew Musial  — Follow Up

rep.name: Andrew Musial
rep.location: Poland — confirmed on this call, 'I'll bring you the goodies from Poland', and the call ran at 2am his time

setter.name: Kim Forbes-Sobers
setter.evidence: The title carries no KFS suffix, but the rep names the setter three times and demonstrably worked from her notes: 'Kim gave me some context. So, you've been working out like weighted calisthenics for a while, yeah?', then 'from Kim, he told me, like, you've been, like, what's been missing is a little bit of structure. Is that correct?', then 'I remember Kim asked you, like, you're from Bahia, right?' Recorded as Kim Forbes-Sobers per the corpus key; the setter code field is left null because the title does not carry one, which is itself a finding — setter attribution in file titles is incomplete.

prospect.name: João Gabriel D.
prospect.location: Brazil — nearest large city Salvador; lives in the top-floor apartment of a building with a small terrace where he trains outdoors
prospect.occupation: Physician. Runs a private practice, works at a hospital, and this year became a professor of medicine teaching students and residents. Works mornings and afternoons every day, formerly including night shifts, dialled back after his first child. Also does research. His wife is also a doctor.
prospect.family_status: Married; his wife is a doctor who runs, does CrossFit and trains three to four times a week. One daughter aged two, and a second daughter due in the last week of October. They recently moved to a larger apartment which is mid-renovation, and expect to hire in-house childcare help to sustain both careers after the birth.
prospect.training_background: Serious calisthenics athlete. Several years of bodyweight calisthenics, close to two years of weighted calisthenics, and he calls himself an intermediate athlete. Current numbers: eight to twelve clean pull-up reps with 20 kg added, and dips with 25 kg added. Started at 69 kg as a very skinny man in his early twenties and has built to 86 kg. Moved from high-volume grinding work to a low-volume programme after developing joint discomfort. Now runs a heavy weighted calisthenics session every four to six days, one standard gym leg day, and two or three kettlebell sessions a week of 20 to 25 minutes. Owns one 16 kg kettlebell, bought after finding Trevor's YouTube channel. Trains 30 to 40 minutes, either before the household wakes or between morning and afternoon clinic. Self-describes as a research nerd on training. Does not like steady-state cardio or bodybuilding-style training.
prospect.medical: Nothing disclosed. No injuries — he was asked directly and answered 'No, injury. I think it was most like overload stuff, overload in the joints and muscles, but I was never injured.' Reports joint ache and stiffness from high-rep calisthenics volume, which prompted his switch to lower volume. Practises fasting of 24 to 36 hours every one to two weeks and reports improved cognitive performance on fasting days.

signals: Already fit and successful and explicitly wants good to great: 'I got to a pretty decent strength level, an intermediate level for a calisthenic athlete, but I was neglecting a lot of stuff in terms of endurance, in terms of VO2 max... I'm not really satisfied with that.' Target body fat 10-12% from a current 13-14%.
Occupation is the ICP's own headline example — a physician with a private practice, a hospital role and a professorship.

Does not devalue the offer at any point; he validates it while declining: 'I don't think it's an absurd value. And I think for that, for Trevor's work and for the accountability, I think actually that is pretty fair.'
Buying structure rather than motivation, which is the optimizer's purchase: 'discipline is not a problem' and 'my mind works very well when I know exactly what to do.'

COUNTER-SIGNAL, and the reason confidence sits at 0.72: for a true optimizer price is a quality signal rather than a barrier, and here price was the only barrier and a genuine one — $6,000 converts to roughly R$25,000-28,000, against a household mid-renovation with a second child due in October and a temporary income dip from restructuring their practice. He is an optimizer priced in the wrong currency, not an optimizer who found the price cheap.

goals.text: Add conditioning and VO2 max, which years of calisthenics-only training have left behind — named as the primary objective alongside muscle
Gain some muscle mass without becoming a bodybuilder — 'I don't want to look like I bought a building'
Drop from 13-14% body fat to 10-12%, not for vanity but because 'when that happened, my training gets a lot better'
Get a structure that combines weighted calisthenics with kettlebells — 'my great doubts nowadays are how to combine those two'
Cut through the noise in the fitness industry and know exactly what to do on which day — 'my mind works very well when I know exactly what to do'
Build mobility, which calisthenics-only training neglects
Keep training effectively in 30 to 40 minute sessions around a hospital schedule and two small children
Have the energy to play with two daughters and perform at work — the reason he named conditioning as the priority
Train in a way that is still sustainable at 50 — 'I don't want to be doing bicep curls when I'm 50'
Build the kind of body Trevor has — 'that body, Trevor's body, it's the way I want to be built... that kind of body is my goal body'

pains.text: No structure for combining kettlebells with weighted calisthenics — the central, self-diagnosed gap: 'mainly for me is structure, is combining with what to do, in what day, for how long'
Too much conflicting information despite extensive research — 'there's a lot of noise in the fitness industry. [With] structure, you can reduce that'
Conditioning, VO2 max and mobility eroded by years of single-goal training — 'a lot of stuff that seems that I was losing through time, just by having only one goal'
Joint discomfort and stiffness from high-volume calisthenics, which forced a programme change
Severe time scarcity — private practice, hospital work, a new professorship, and a two-year-old, leaving 'sometimes just half an hour, 40 minutes to work out'
A second child due in October that he expects to cut training to a minimum, based on experience — 'sometimes we're two or three days without sleeping well'
Household finances committed to an apartment renovation, incoming childcare costs, rising school fees and a temporary income dip from restructuring their practice
Cannot train for an hour or more any more and does not believe it would be healthy at 33 with a young family

objections.raw_quote: I still would like something that would give me the possibility of continuing to train weighted calisthenics, which is something that I really like to do... I don't know if that's possible to combine them, but that would be my primary will is to combine those things. To not lose the gains in strength in calisthenics, but add something new.
objections.rep_response: Answered it directly and well, twice. First: 'critically for you, the kettlebell days and calisthenics days, they complement each other naturally. So you don't have to replace anything that you've built. You're adding the pieces that you've been actually missing.' Then when it resurfaced at 00:42:49 he pointed at Trevor's own content — Trevor does pull-ups, dips and leg raises — and closed with 'this is tailored to your needs, whatever you will discuss with Trevor, he will build a program around that.' The prospect visibly moved on and softened his own requirement: 'it could be calisthenics, like raw calisthenics bodyweight, if it's going to give me muscles... it's fine.' Proposed label for this objection type: training_compatibility.

objections.raw_quote: that for me right now I believe that is a little bit out of our budget right now I believe, because when we have to deal in Brazilian [reais], when we make the conversion it's about probably something along the lines of 25 to 28,000... So I don't think I can split that into payments right now.
objections.rep_response: Isolated properly — 'just make sure, apart from the finances right now, is there anything standing in a way from moving forward?' — and got a clean answer. Offered two-, three- and six-payment structures with the interest disclosed transparently, then down-sold to a three-month tier at $4,000 with a $2,000 x 2 or $1,500 x 3 split. Finally attempted a down payment: 'be transparent. Like, how much would you be actually willing to put down today?' The prospect declined to name a figure. None of the financial-picture questions were asked.

objections.raw_quote: we already committed to a lot of expenses right now due to we moving to a different apartment... the apartment actually needs some restructuring, like infrastructure stuff. So already committed to that, and I think there will be a lot of expense in the next four to five months... we may be dealing with a couple of months that money will be a little shorter than it usually is because of that restructuring [of the private practice].
objections.rep_response: Ran one good move — 'what's going to change between now and sometime in the future?' — and got a specific, credible answer about the renovation completing and saving resuming. He then asked for a timeframe, got 'I don't really have a concrete answer for you', and settled for a call in one month rather than pressing on the fact that the named obstacle resolves on a schedule.

objections.raw_quote: August, September, and October will be difficult months for me because my wife will be very pregnant. And the moment that the little princess is gonna come to this world is probably in the last week of October. So I don't think that in this moment, I'll have to deal with a lot of stuff and probably training will be kept to a minimum, or maybe even severely impaired.
objections.rep_response: First instinct was to dismiss it with the accountability pillar — 'that's why Trevor is for you there when life gets busy' — and the prospect corrected him firmly: 'I don't believe it's actually busy. I believe it's actually probably not only busy, but tiredness and lack of sleep.' The second instinct was much better and genuinely creative: reframe the timeline so the engagement fits the good months. 'We're in almost June. So it's June, July, August, and you have a lot of time till October. We could do the three months.' That was the right structural answer and it still could not overcome the currency problem.

objections.raw_quote: I don't know if I can really can do that right now so I have to take a little moment to think about that and involve the wife because we have a lot of projects now for this year.
objections.rep_response: None. The wife was never mentioned again for the remaining twenty-three minutes of the call. No attempt to bring her into the conversation, no question about what objection she might raise, and no use of the fact — already established in discovery — that she is herself a doctor who runs, does CrossFit and trains three to four times a week.

objections.raw_quote: Is there a possibility, Andrew, that I could get in touch with you after some time and maybe we can talk again about this? Is there this possibility?
objections.rep_response: Did not simply grant it — he asked what would change, asked for a timeframe, and asked what the prospect would put down today, which is the right order of moves. But with no number forthcoming he agreed to a call a full month out, on 29 June, with no deposit, no interim commitment and nothing to be done in between.

offer.payment_plan_terms: Quoted transparently with the premium disclosed. Against the $6,000 six-month tier: one-time payment, or two payments of the the $500–$1,000 band+ band, or three- and six-payment plans where 'the overall price is higher' — six payments of $1,200 for a $7,200 total. Against the $4,000 three-month tier: two payments of $2,000 or three payments of the $1,000–$2,500 band. Credit card is the default method: 'Usually people just put it on a credit card.' Note the rep proactively volunteered that instalments cost more, which is better practice than any other call in this batch.
offer.guarantee_mentioned: Stated for the first time in this corpus and attached only to the six-month tier: 'with six months, you have a guarantee that you will definitely gain at least 20, it's pounds, so it's going to be like around plus 10 kilos from the baseline that you start with on weight of kettlebells.' Explicitly not available on the shorter tier: 'with three months, we cannot guarantee that, because it's too short. I think it's too short for every fitness goal.'

evidence: No payment, no payment link, no verbal agreement. The prospect declined both tiers on affordability: 'that for me right now I believe that is a little bit out of our budget' and, on the $4,000 option, 'it's a lot for right now, even 4K, because that will mean something close to 20,000 [reais].'

He asked for the conversation to be resumed later rather than closed out — 'Is there a possibility that I could get in touch with you after some time and maybe we can talk again about this?' — and a concrete call was booked for 29 June at 8pm Brazil time, 1am for the rep.
Contact details were exchanged and a WhatsApp message was sent and received during the call, so the relationship is live rather than dormant.

Strong buying signals throughout: he validated the price rather than resisting it ('I don't think it's an absurd value... for Trevor's work and for the accountability, I think actually that is pretty fair'), named cost as the single obstacle when isolated, and confirmed 'I have the time and I have the will.'

Counter-evidence, and it is structural rather than motivational: the obstacle is currency and life stage, not desire. $6,000 lands as roughly R$25,000-28,000; the household is mid-renovation with committed costs, a second child due in the last week of October, rising school fees, an expected childcare hire, and a temporary income dip from restructuring their private practice. He explicitly declined to name any amount he could put down today because 'things are changing too fast right now.'

Also counter-evidence on the follow-up date: the call was set a full month out with no deposit and no interim step, and the prospect's own timeline says his finances will not clarify until after October.
outcome.next_step: Follow-up call booked for Monday 29 June at 8pm Brazil time (1am in Poland; the rep offered to move it and the prospect said his own hours were fine). Rep to send a calendar invite and will contact him on WhatsApp rather than SMS. No action assigned to the prospect beyond gaining clarity on the household budget.

notable.note: The most important ICP data point in the batch, and a set of firsts on the offer. FINDINGS. (1) THE ICP'S OWN HEADLINE EXAMPLE FAILED ON PRICE. The stated ICP says 'they own their own business, or they're a physician'. This is the corpus's first actual physician — private practice, hospital post, professorship, wife also a doctor — and he could not afford $6,000, or $4,000, because it converts to R$25,000-28,000. The ICP names a profession without accounting for geography, and the finding is that 'makes good money' is not a property of an occupation, it is a property of an occupation in a currency. (2) FIRST STATEMENT OF THE GUARANTEE ANYWHERE IN THIS CORPUS: a gain of at least 20 lb (about 10 kg) on kettlebell working weight from baseline, available only on the six-month tier and explicitly withheld from the three-month tier. It appears in no other call in this batch, including calls where the same rep sold the same six-month tier. Someone should confirm the guarantee's real terms and why it is not being stated consistently. (3) THE $4,000 THREE-MONTH TIER APPEARS FOR THE THIRD TIME in four days from the same rep, and here he recommended it — after having just told the prospect that three months is 'too short for every fitness goal' and carries no guarantee. Whatever the tier's status, recommending the ungruaranteed option minutes after arguing it is too short to work is a positioning problem. (4) PAYMENT PLANS ARE REAL AND STRUCTURED: two, three and six payments, with six at $1,200 x 6 for $7,200. Identical to the structures quoted to Marian S. the day before, and inconsistent with what the same rep told two earlier prospects, that Primal has no set payment plans. He also proactively disclosed that instalments cost more, which no other call in this batch does. (5) THE REP'S IDENTITY IS RESOLVED HERE. At 01:04:17 the prospect asks how to pronounce his surname, transcribed 'Muschau', which is how Musiał is pronounced, and the rep adds 'actually it's not Andrew, it's Andrzej, but nobody can pronounce it, so I go by Andrew.' Combined with Poland, the closer role and the Drive folder, this confirms the 'Andrew Jin (Primal Instinct)' label belongs to Andrew Musial. (6) AN UNDISCLOSED AI SMS AGENT IS CONTACTING PROSPECTS. 'I've been receiving messages like SMS messages from someone named Sophia... I thought it was an AI. But when I try to respond to that, sometimes she asks me to respond yes or no. I don't believe that the SMS is coming through.' The rep confirmed it is a bot only after being asked. Two issues: the persona is not disclosed as automated up front, and SMS to Brazil is not being delivered, matching the international SMS limitation described on the internal Close training call. (7) BIGGEST COACHING MISS: the wife objection was raised and never touched, despite the rep having already established that she is a doctor who runs, does CrossFit and trains three to four times a week — the most winnable spouse objection in the corpus, left entirely unused.

quality.notes: Pervasive inversion, worst in the second half. Roles read from content throughout. Examples: at 00:02:36 'Two years. And I consider myself, yeah, I consider myself now more of an intermediate athlete' merges the rep's echo with the prospect's answer under the rep's label; at 00:03:20 the rep's interjection 'Sorry to interject, did you had any injuries doing that?' is split across two labels; at 00:10:57 'How much muscle you would like to gain?' sits under the prospect but is the rep; and from roughly 00:44:06 to 00:47:00 the transcript collapses into long unpunctuated blocks that contain both speakers, including the price statement itself — 'the investment is six thousand dollars one-time payment okay let me just uh take note of that' — where the quote is the rep's and the acknowledgement is the prospect's. The $6,000, $4,000 and $7,200 figures are all recoverable with confidence from surrounding context. The surname exchange at 01:04:17-01:04:28 is also inverted, with the rep's question and the prospect's reply both landing oddly, but the content is unambiguous. Connection quality was poor at the start with a freeze around 00:00:57, and there is a two-minute gap from 00:58:33 to 01:00:20 while the prospect checked a calendar. Overall audio was otherwise clear.

P1.evidence: P1a hit, and among the best in the batch — the rep had demonstrably read the setter's notes and used them three separate times: 'Kim gave me some context. So, you've been working out like weighted calisthenics for a while, yeah?', then 'from Kim, he told me, like, you've been, what's been missing is a little bit of structure. Is that correct?', then the rapport-building 'I remember Kim asked you, like, you're from Bahia, right?' He also opened by acknowledging the prospect's situation — 'I know you're juggling a lot with the hospital schedule and family.' P1b partial and the thinnest frame in the batch: 'Before we dive in, just want to make sure I actually understand your situation. So, before we get into any details about the program.' That is one of four parts plus a sequencing promise; where he wants to go, what is in the way and what he needs were all unframed. P1c hit — 'Cool?' asked and answered. P1d miss, and it is a direct consequence of P1a going well: having read the notes, the rep opened with closed confirmation questions off those notes rather than an open invitation. There is no version of 'what are you looking for help with' or 'brief me in your own words' anywhere on this call. It worked out because the prospect is articulate and volunteered freely, but the script credits asking.

P2.evidence: P2a partial — height, weight and age were all volunteered inside other answers and none was asked; the rep did however ask the more useful question for this prospect, 'Have you measured your fat tissue?', which produced 13-14% and a 10-12% target. P2b hit — occupation came from the setter notes and was then properly explored: 'you as a doctor, you probably work long hours, or not?' followed by the actual daily shape of the schedule. P2c miss — no health conditions or hereditary screen at all. P2d hit and promptly asked at the right moment: the prospect mentioned joint discomfort and the rep interrupted with 'Sorry to interject, did you had any injuries doing that?' P2e hit, and the best moment of the baseline: given a tangled answer about rotating splits, the rep refused to accept it — 'Jesus Christ, I got lost. So how many days do you work out per week, every day?' — and got a usable picture. P2f hit — current results were established in detail, both the wins (69 kg to 86 kg, 8-12 pull-ups with +20 kg) and the deficits (VO2 max, endurance, mobility). P2g hit — 'tell me about nutrition, how does it look like right now?', then the cheat-meal probes, which surfaced the fasting protocol. P2h miss, and conspicuously: sleep was never asked, on a physician with a two-year-old and a newborn due — and sleep deprivation is exactly the obstacle the prospect himself raised forty minutes later as the reason the programme might not work in October. P2i partial — energy was touched only inside the body-fat exchange, never established as a baseline.

P3.evidence: P3a hit — the one-thing question was asked with a time horizon attached: 'which one of these would be the most important thing for you? Like in six months, if you had to choose.' P3b hit and near-verbatim, offering the menu explicitly: 'You mentioned VO2 max, conditioning, mobility, probably too. So which one of these would be the most important thing for you?' P3c miss — never asked what he wants to do physically and cannot. P3d hit, and it was the single most productive question on the call: 'Why conditioning is so important?' opened the entire life context — busy doctor, second child coming, shrinking free time. P3e hit — 'if we get it dialed in, get you a structure, a proper plan... when you think about, what would be different? How would you operate if you would have the dial-in?' P3f partial — 'What does your wife say about it?' is a good adjacent question about support rather than impact, and the impact on the daughters was asserted by the rep in the pitch rather than asked. P3g partial — kids, marriage and the long run all appeared and the prospect supplied the material himself ('I don't want to be doing bicep curls when I'm 50'); the rep echoed rather than drove. P3h hit — an accurate, confirmed reflect-back: 'just to summarize, you told me that you've been missing some pieces, that you've been researching that, and there's been a lot of noise out there... and that the missing piece was the conditioning and mobility part and getting more VO2 max, but at the same time you build a solid strength for yourself with the heavy calisthenics.'

P4.evidence: The second clean sweep of this phase in the batch, both by the same rep in two days. P4a and P4b hit — the full training history was elicited and so was its consequence: high-volume grinding calisthenics produced joint ache and stiffness, which forced the switch to low-volume work. P4c, P4d and P4f were all delivered by one exceptionally well-built question at 00:17:10, which is the scripted 'information isn't the problem' move adapted precisely to this prospect: 'you clearly have, like, you know your stuff, yeah? So you've researched training extensively, and you've been doing this for years. So what's held you back from getting that conditioning and mobility piece dialed in on your own?' Asking a research-obsessed doctor why his own research has not solved it is exactly right, and it is the same move the rep failed to run on Jared L. the previous day. P4e hit — the prospect named his own gap cleanly and twice: 'mainly for me is structure, is combining with what to do, in what day, for how long, and what to do' and 'there's a lot of noise in the fitness industry. [With] structure, you can reduce that. So I believe that is what I'm lacking right now.' Getting the prospect to say the word 'structure' unprompted is the phase landing perfectly.

P5.evidence: Not run in any form — no two-year question, no settling question, no 'why not', no line in the sand. The material was on the table and unused: the prospect twice described losing ground, 'a lot of stuff that seems that I was losing through time, just by having only one goal', and closed it with 'I'm not really satisfied with that.' That is an invitation to ask what another two years of the same looks like, at 33, with a second child arriving and less time than ever. Instead the rep moved straight from the reflect-back into the three pillars. This is the recurring pattern across the batch and it matters most here, because when the price landed there was no accumulated cost of inaction for it to be weighed against — only a currency conversion.

P6.evidence: P6a partial — the belief question was never asked in the scripted form. The nearest approach, at 00:24:09, tests willingness rather than belief: 'if we could build a system that would fit around your hospital working hours and that could preserve your calisthenics and actually give you the conditioning and mobility, is this something that you're really actually wanting to commit right now?' P6b hit, verbatim and correctly placed before any number: 'if you had all those three things, like the structure, kettlebell programming built around your calisthenics, the nutrition dialed in, and someone who is in your corner supporting you all the way, would there be any reason you wouldn't commit to this?' The answer was 'Mainly cost', and the rep isolated immediately with 'Apart from that' — producing a clean 'I don't think there is another variable that concerns me.' That is the phase working. P6c partial — a second commitment check ran before pricing ('if you can figure out the details, the investment side, you're fully committed to showing up and doing the work?' / 'Yeah. I'm really looking forward to that'), which is correct sequencing. But the prospect had already named cost as the blocker fifteen minutes earlier, and the rep proceeded to the number without doing anything to pre-frame it or return to Phase 5 — which had never been run. Knowing the objection in advance and walking into it unprepared is the shortfall here.

P11.evidence: A close was attempted — two tiers priced, four payment structures offered, a down payment requested — but no agreement to buy was obtained, so payment collection, the Trevor onboarding booking, the agreement signature and the welcome sequence were all unreachable. Scored N/A rather than miss so the phase does not double-count the unresolved affordability objection.

objection_plays.detail: Good structure, no financial picture. ISOLATE FIRST ran twice and cleanly — first inside the Phase 6 check ('Mainly cost' / 'Apart from that'), then again after the number: 'just make sure, apart from the finances right now, is there anything standing in a way from moving forward?' The payment door was opened with real, specific structures rather than vagueness — two payments of the the $500–$1,000 band+ band, three- and six-payment plans, and the six-pay total of $7,200 named out loud — and the rep proactively disclosed that instalments cost more, which no other call in this batch does and which is genuinely good practice. He then down-sold to the three-month tier at $4,000 with its own splits. The strongest single move came at 00:55:30: 'be transparent. Like, how much would you be actually willing to put down today? Just to see how it looks like.' That is the right question and it failed only because the prospect genuinely did not know. What never ran: permission for an open financial conversation, and every one of the six financial-picture items — cash on hand, monthly surplus after bills, number of credit cards, available credit per card, used versus available, and crypto or investments. He learned the qualitative picture (renovation commitments, incoming childcare costs, school fees, a temporary income dip) and never converted it into numbers, so the down-payment question arrived with nothing behind it.

The clearest single coaching miss in this batch. The trigger was explicit at 00:45:06 — 'I have to take a little moment to think about that and involve the wife because we have a lot of projects now for this year' — and the wife was never mentioned again across the remaining twenty-three minutes. Not one move ran: no 'money aside, do you personally feel this CAN get you there', no 'when you talk to her, what obstacles might come up', no 'is there any reason she would NOT want you stronger', no offer to include her on the follow-up, and no deposit-with-refund fallback. What makes it costly is that the rep had already done the hard part in discovery: he knew the wife is a doctor who runs, does CrossFit and trains three to four times a week, and who gets frustrated when she cannot train twice a week. That is a spouse who would plainly endorse the purchase, and the rep had her profile in hand and did not use a word of it. He also never suggested she join the 29 June call, despite the prospect having framed the decision as joint.

Triggered twice and handled unevenly. The first trigger was the pregnancy window — 'August, September, and October will be difficult months... training will be kept to a minimum, or maybe even severely impaired.' The rep's opening move was the wrong one, waving it away with the accountability pillar ('that's why Trevor is for you there when life gets busy'), and the prospect corrected him: 'I don't believe it's actually busy. I believe it's actually probably not only busy, but tiredness and lack of sleep... sometimes we're two or three days without sleeping well.' His recovery was genuinely good and unscripted: rather than arguing, he restructured the offer to fit the available window — 'we're in almost June. So it's June, July, August, and you have a lot of time till October. We could do the three months.' That is the right instinct and it deserves credit. The second trigger was the deferral request, and there he ran the play's core question well — 'what's going to change between now and sometime in the future?' Not run: 'things never slow down', 'when does it actually become the right time', 'the longer you wait the harder this gets', and 'the only thing you can control is right now'. The last of these had obvious purchase on a man who had just said he does not know what his finances look like after October.

Trigger present — 'I have to take a moment to think about that' and later 'Is there a possibility that I could get in touch with you after some time?' To his credit the rep did not simply grant it: he asked what would change, asked for a timeframe, and asked what the prospect would put down today, which is three consecutive attempts to convert a delay into a decision. None of the scripted lines ran — no 'do you feel what we've gone through CAN get you to [goal]', no 'thinking isn't the problem, deciding is', no 'the way you've been approaching this brought you here, when do you make a different decision', no closing 'are you sure? Nothing else keeping you from being 100% in?' The outcome is a call booked a full month out with no deposit, no interim commitment and nothing for the prospect to do in between, against his own statement that his finances will not clarify until after October.

SCRIPT GAP — foreign currency conversion, and this is now the third occurrence in four sales calls in this batch. 'When we make the conversion it's about probably something along the lines of 25 to 28,000 [reais]' for $6,000, and on the reduced tier, 'it's a lot for right now, even 4K, because that will mean something close to 20,000.' The rep did not acknowledge the conversion once. The same gap appeared with a New Zealand prospect converting to NZ$7,500 and with a Danish prospect weighing $9,000 against local salaries. Primal is selling a flat USD price into markets with very different purchasing power and the playbook has no move for it, no regional pricing, and no framing that addresses it. On this call it is the sole reason a textbook-ICP physician did not buy.

SECOND SCRIPT GAP — a dated life event with a real physiological consequence, as distinct from the generic busyness Objection D is built for. A newborn arriving in the last week of October is not an excuse, it is a scheduled period of sleep deprivation that the prospect has already lived through once. Objection D's moves ('are you ever going to have another Thanksgiving?', 'things never slow down') are actively wrong here and would have read as dismissive, which is exactly what happened when the rep reached for the accountability pillar. What is needed and does not exist: a documented pause or hold mechanism, or a start date deliberately timed to the window before the birth. The rep improvised the second of those and it was the right answer — it simply arrived attached to a price the prospect could not pay.

THIRD GAP, recorded because it was handled well without a script — training compatibility. The prospect's stated primary condition was that he keep progressing weighted calisthenics: 'that would be my primary will is to combine those things. To not lose the gains in strength in calisthenics.' No play exists for a prospect who fears the programme will displace training he already values. The rep answered it properly and twice: 'the kettlebell days and calisthenics days, they complement each other naturally. So you don't have to replace anything that you've built. You're adding the pieces that you've been actually missing', and then with proof from Trevor's own content showing pull-ups, dips and leg raises. The objection resolved — the prospect visibly relaxed his own requirement, 'it could be calisthenics, like raw calisthenics bodyweight... it's fine.' Worth codifying as a play, since it will recur with any prospect who already has a training identity.

adherence.notes: Strong discovery, no urgency, and a loss to currency rather than to selling. The front two-thirds are among the best in the batch: setter notes genuinely used, a baseline that refused to accept vague answers, the full goals phase run properly, and a clean sweep on root cause built around one excellent question — asking a research-obsessed physician why his own research has not solved the problem. He also took commitment before the number and isolated the objection cleanly. Three things to coach. First, Phase 5 was not run at all, and this prospect handed over the material for it twice by describing capacity he has been losing over time; with no cost of inaction established, the price had nothing to be weighed against. Second, the wife objection was raised and completely ignored, despite the rep already knowing she is a CrossFitting doctor who trains three to four times a week — the most winnable spouse objection in the corpus, left untouched, and she was not invited to the follow-up. Third, the follow-up was set a month out with no deposit and no interim step, against the prospect's own statement that clarity will not arrive until after October; a booked call in five months with a deposit today would have been the stronger ask. Escalate above the rep: this is the ICP's headline occupation — a physician — declining on affordability purely because $6,000 converts to R$25,000-28,000. That is the third foreign-currency loss in four sales calls in this batch and there is no play, no framing and no regional pricing for it.

quality.notes: Swaps concentrated in short exchanges. The long clinical monologue is clearly the prospect and is reliably attributed. A 3-minute silent gap at 00:09-00:13 suggests audio loss.

P1.evidence: Second call in a sequence, so the frame belongs to call one. Did open by reading back where they left off and checking what stood out — the right move for a continuation.

P2.evidence: Baseline was gathered on call one, which is a separate transcript not in this pilot.

P3.evidence: Re-asked the goal — 'walk me through the goal, paint me the picture one more time' — but took the surface answer (lose weight, mobility, core strength, avoid falls) and did not drive to the deeper why. On a call where the prospect had just been emotionally deflated by his physio, the deeper why was the available lever and it was not pulled.

P4.evidence: Covered on call one.

P5.evidence: No consequence frame — notable because the prospect's own clinical trajectory (arthritis, possible surgery, 30 years of compensation) is the strongest consequence case in the pilot and went entirely unused.

objection_plays.detail: Fear of harm was present — 'they're not sure if me swinging around is the best idea.' The rep used a partial-value reframe and a good path-to-yes question ('what would be the route to getting you back to swinging stuff around?'), but ran none of the scripted OE moves: no certainty question, no bridge, no plane, no burned-before.

The dominant objection was clinical program fit — the physio ruled out swings, snatches, cleans, Turkish get-ups, overhead presses, push press, windmills and high pulls. The script has no play for this. The rep improvised reasonably and escalated to Trevor, which is defensible, but it is unscripted territory.

adherence.notes: Scored on observable phases only. The real finding here is a script gap rather than a rep gap: the playbook has no clinical-objection path, and this prospect's blocker was 100% clinical.

P1.evidence: Warm, rapport-led open — 'what got you interested in doing this too?' No four-part frame, no frame agreement, no notes read back.

P2.evidence: The most complete baseline in the pilot. Height 5'5", weight 144, work status, scoliosis, shoulder dislocation, knee tendonitis, depression history, full nutrition and intermittent-fasting detail, extended sleep discussion. Never asked age.

P3.evidence: 'If you could change one thing about how you feel or move?' → stability and balance → 'spread to other parts of my life' → probed that → confidence → dancing, hiking, pregnancy, old age. Clean reflect-back: 'this goes much further than only losing extra pounds.'

P4.evidence: The prospect volunteered the root cause unprompted — 'whenever I've gone and done any other programs, I don't even know if I'm doing this right.' The rep never asked what she had tried, what happened, or why it didn't stick. Phase effectively skipped.

P5.evidence: No consequence frame at any point. Cost of inaction never made real.

P6.evidence: 'If you had everything that you needed, do you feel genuinely that you're going to get to your goals?' → 'Yes.' → 'No hesitation.' Clean verbal yes before presenting.

P11.evidence: Payment confirmed live — 'that went through.' Trevor call booked Monday 11:15 MT. Agreement was promised for later by email rather than signed on the call. Onboarding form mentioned as a follow-up; no Skool link or welcome-email instruction given.

objection_plays.detail: No money, timing, spouse, think-about-it or fear objection was ever raised. The only concern was a pregnancy plan, handled with a reframe plus the pause guarantee. This is what a pre-framed warm referral looks like.

adherence.notes: Closed on the strength of discovery and a warm referral despite skipping phases 4 and 5 entirely. Demonstrates that a pre-sold prospect masks script gaps — which is exactly why close rate alone is a poor coaching signal.

notable.note: Pricing deviation and a refund. A previously collected $100 deposit was returned on this call. A non-standard Primal University tier was offered at $200/month or $1,000/6 months, and the rep then misquoted the plan total as $1,200 for the same six months. The rep also disqualified on ethics rather than pressing — 'the last thing that we want to do is put someone in an even worse financial position' — which is defensible but means no objection play was run at all. Prospect is mid-recovery from a serious accident with brain involvement; medical spend dwarfs the offer.

quality.notes: Frequent inversions. At 00:00:33 the prospect's block opens with the rep's question 'How does it look like for you?'; at 00:04:49 a rep line ('the cards that you've been dealt and that needs a workaround') is attributed to the prospect; at 00:11:09 and 00:14:16 rep and prospect lines are merged into single blocks. Role was read from content throughout.

P1.evidence: Warm, well-built rapport open (the restaurant cap, praise for his drive) and a clean open question — 'So take me through, what were your thoughts?' — but no four-part frame and no frame agreement. Defensible on a continuation call, though the rep never reset expectations for what this call was for.

P2.evidence: Second call in a sequence; baseline was taken previously. No baseline re-run and none expected.

P3.evidence: No goal work at all. The prospect volunteered real depth unprompted — the proposal, the wedding, his shape and shoulder, family support — and the rep never connected any of it to an outcome. He never asked what moving better would do for him or who else it impacts, despite a fiancée and a family business sitting right there.

P4.evidence: No past-attempts or root-cause work. The prospect mentioned he had been doing kettlebells and stretching on his own for a few days — an obvious opening to ask why self-directed effort has not stuck — and the rep only used it as encouragement.

P5.evidence: No consequence frame. Nothing about what the next two years look like if the recovery plateaus, no line-in-the-sand. This was the phase that could have changed the call and it was skipped entirely.

P6.evidence: Money was isolated in substance — 'if the money would be there... you would be like, yes, let's go for it, but it sounds like that's the only thing that's stopping you at the moment, right?' — which the prospect confirmed. But belief was never tested (P6a) and the isolation came after the offer, not before. He correctly did not push forward without a yes.

P11.evidence: No agreement was reached on any tier, so payment and onboarding were never reachable. The only payment event was outbound — the rep initiated a refund of the previously collected $100.

objection_plays.detail: Isolation ran ('if the money would be there... that's the only thing stopping you'). Two financial-picture questions ran: monthly leftover after bills, and cash available now. Everything else was skipped — no 'you're not in a SHOULD I place, you're in a HOW place', no credit cards, no available credit, no crypto/stocks/investments, and no explicit 'are you comfortable having an open honest conversation about where you're at financially'. The rep also pre-conceded the outcome out loud — 'I don't think it's going to work anyway, but just trying to get every' — which kills the play before the answer arrives.

'I would have to think about it' at 00:09:59. None of the OA moves ran — no 'do you feel what we've gone through can get you to your goal', no 'thinking isn't the problem, deciding is', no 'what's actually coming up that's preventing you from getting started'. The rep instead validated the hesitation and moved to close the call down.

The prospect had already consulted his girlfriend and parents and reported their pushback was financial. The rep asked the useful diagnostic — 'were they overall supportive of it, but it was just the financials?' — and got a yes, then dropped it. No 'is there any reason she would not want you stronger and less in pain', no ownership question, no deposit-and-go-talk-to-her fallback.

Script gap: competing medical spend. The blocker was not capacity to pay in general but that active accident rehab — up to three therapists, hospital bills, medications, with costs about to rise again — outranks training in his budget, and he said so directly: 'the health for my brain and my health in general is a little bit more important for me'. OC assumes discretionary money can be found; there is no play for a prospect whose money is already committed to clinical care he cannot defer. Worth adding to known_gaps_in_script.

adherence.notes: Richard handled a hard human situation with real integrity — he refunded the deposit and refused to worsen the prospect's finances — but he ran almost no process. Phases 3, 4 and 5 were skipped entirely, so when money surfaced there was no consequence or emotional weight for the price to sit against, and the downsell landed as pure cost rather than as a solution. Coach the sequence: on a follow-up close call, re-anchor the goal and the cost of inaction before touching the number, and finish the OC financial picture instead of narrating out loud that it will not work.
